Module: Copilot in Practice Difficulty: Intermediate Prerequisites: Sessions M1-01 to M1-03 Duration: 3 hours (1 hr trainer content + 2 hr lab)

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: Use the standalone copilot CLI to take over one small Node.js project. Inspect commands, revise a plan, then fix the project. Then inspect live fleet results, automate a health report, and compare terminal and IDE workflows. You work in agent-tasks throughout.

docs.title: Learning outcomes
docs.text:
• Install and configure the copilot CLI.
  • Use interactive copilot and copilot -p "...".
  • Use Standard, Plan, and Autopilot modes for multi-step tasks.
  • Revise a /plan before approval and trace it to the diff.
  • Check a /rubber-duck critique.
  • Inspect permissions, sandbox policy, and the soft AI-credit limit.
  • Queue a follow-up, background a command, and read its real result.
  • Recover a disposable edit and tell fork, worktree, move, and resume apart.
  • Use /fleet and /tasks for independent analysis, then check results and usage.
  • Tell JSONL events from an answer payload in programmatic output.
  • Compare CLI, IDE Chat, IDE Agent Mode, and Copilot App workflows.

docs.title: Session materials
docs.text: Resource Location Lab exercises lab/ Lab starter files lab/starter/ Lab solution files lab/solution/

docs.title: Key topics
docs.text:
• Standalone copilot binary: installation, authentication, configuration
  • Interactive prompts for command explanations; copilot -p "..." for command generation
  • Shell integrations: aliases, completion, inline invocation
  • Agent mode for multi-step terminal tasks
  • Copilot App orientation, with plugins and canvas extensions in Session M3-01
  • Cross-IDE comparison: VS Code, Visual Studio, JetBrains, Eclipse, Xcode, and others
  • When to use the CLI, IDE Chat, IDE Agent Mode, or the Copilot App
  • SSH and remote workflows where the CLI is the only option
  • Scripting with Copilot: generating and debugging shell scripts
  • What context the CLI sends
  • Recovery and session controls without broadening permissions

docs.title: Choose the surface that fits the work
docs.text: Session M2-01 | 3 hours

docs.title: Agenda
docs.text: Segment Time CLI fit and setup 10 min Modes and checked plan critique 10 min Programmatic use 10 min Agents and fleet supervision 10 min Controls, queue, and recovery 10 min Surface choice and handoff 10 min

docs.title: Start with the task
docs.text:
Choose the CLI when the work starts or ends in the terminal:

  • reading logs or command output;
  • working over SSH or in a container;
  • running a repeatable command sequence;
  • producing output for another script.

Use the IDE when visual navigation and diff review matter more.

docs.title: Match the mode to the risk
docs.text:
Mode Use it when Standard The task is small or still changing Plan You want to review the approach before edits Autopilot The task has clear limits and a recovery plan

Permissions still apply. More autonomy needs a narrower task.

docs.title: Revise the plan before accepting it
docs.text:
/plan Find the three failing behaviors. Name the files and tests for each fix.
Do not edit project files.

Add a constraint: preserve the response fields and status codes. Ask which steps change. Check the diff before approval.

Save both plans and the assumption you challenged.

docs.title: Ask a different critic before approval
docs.text:
/rubber-duck Critique the repair plan against the source and tests.
Look for a hidden defect or response-contract change. Do not edit files.

Rubber duck is built in and read-only. Copilot selects a contrasting model when one is available. Check the findings yourself.

Inspect /subagents Proactive invocation and leave it unchanged. The opt-in persists and adds usage.

docs.title: Fleet needs independent work
docs.text:
Plan separate read-only questions about routes, utilities, and test gaps.

  1. Leave Plan mode and run /fleet with that breakdown.
  2. Open /tasks and read the child-task results.
  3. Check claims against files or focused tests.
  4. Reconcile disagreements and inspect /usage.

Extra agents can use more credits.

docs.title: Shared commands, different surfaces
docs.text: Workflow Surface /plan, /fleet, /review CLI and app /orchestrate App built-in skill; Session M7-05 copilot -p and shell pipelines CLI Cloud changes through /delegate Session M3-02

docs.title: State the limits of an automated task
docs.text:
• the working directory;
  • the files or commands in scope;
  • the expected result;
  • the checks to run;
  • when Copilot must stop.

docs.title: Programmatic mode needs a contract
docs.text:
copilot -p "Summarize the failing test output"

Before another script uses the answer, define:

  • stable input;
  • a predictable output format;
  • a failure signal;
  • limited permissions.

--output-format=json emits JSONL events. Parsing each line doesn't show that the task succeeded or that the answer fits your schema.

docs.title: CLI and IDE can share one workflow
docs.text:
CLI
  reproduce the failure
  capture focused test output
        ↓
IDE
  inspect the code and diff
  review the proposed change
        ↓
CLI
  rerun checks
  record the result

Switch surfaces when the work changes.

docs.title: Inspect approval, sandbox, and limit separately
docs.text:
/permissions show
/sandbox status
/sandbox policy node --version
/limits

Approval decides whether a tool may run. The sandbox limits process access. Inspect both without weakening them.

AI-credit caps are soft. GitHub's references differ on reset scope, so check what your installed UI shows.

docs.title: Queue, stash, and background are different
docs.text:
Control Result Ctrl+Q Queue a follow-up while busy Ctrl+S Stash or restore an unsent draft Ctrl+X, b Move a running command to the background /tasks Show its state, output, and exit status

Use the lab's harmless 15-second command. Compare the queued summary with the real result. Background work stays in the CLI session and doesn't isolate files.

docs.title: Recover before branching an alternative
docs.text:
1. Commit the checked repair.
  2. Let Copilot create only a disposable note.
  3. Open /rewind and restore conversation and files.
  4. Check the note is gone and the repair remains.

Rewind doesn't undo external actions or replace Git rollback.

docs.title: Context fork is not file isolation
docs.text:
Command Result /fork Conversation fork, same files /fork worktree Context plus a new checkout of HEAD /worktree New checkout; uncommitted edits stay behind /move Move the uncommitted draft into a new worktree /resume Return to the parent; check its path, branch, and status

Move only the analysis note. Don't merge the alternative.

docs.title: Save the work for review
docs.text:
Keep:

  • the final diff;
  • test output and exit status;
  • generated reports;
  • the prompts you used.

Another engineer should be able to check the work without the conversation.

docs.title: Lab handoff
docs.text:
Use /plan, challenge an assumption, and approve the revision before the repair. Read /fleet results through /tasks and check the claims you accept. Check the critique against the source. Note the controls, the queue and background result, and the recovery and worktree state.

120 minutes: setup 15; repair 40; programmatic and fleet 35; recovery and choice 30.

Submit: passing tests, a reviewed diff, the health report, and workflow-record.md with the plan revision and usage.

docs.title: Lab
docs.text: Overview Lab Trainer Guide

docs.title: Session M2-01 lab: GitHub Copilot in the CLI
docs.text:
Duration: 2 hours

Deliverable: A reviewed agent-tasks project, a project health script, and a CLI workflow cheat sheet

docs.title: Lab overview
docs.text:
You take over the agent-tasks Node.js project. Use the standalone CLI to inspect its commands, repair it, and automate a health report. Then decide whether the CLI or the IDE fits each task. Use synthetic data only.

Exercise Topic Time 1 CLI setup and first commands 15 min 2 Plan, revise, and repair 40 min 3 Programmatic output and fleet 35 min 4 Recovery, isolated alternatives, and surface choice 30 min

docs.title: You need
docs.text:
• the standalone Copilot CLI with a signed-in GitHub account that has Copilot;
  • GitHub CLI (gh), Node.js 22 or later, and Git with a local commit identity;
  • the local sandbox, enabled;
  • VS Code for the final comparison.

In the CLI, check that /help lists /plan, /rubber-duck, /subagents, /fleet, /tasks, /permissions, /sandbox, /limits, /rewind, /fork, /move, and /resume. Quick help lists the queue and background shortcuts.

gh --version        # 2.x or higher
node --version      # v22 or higher
gh auth status      # Logged in to github.com

If gh auth status says you're not logged in, run gh auth login, choose HTTPS, and sign in through the browser.

docs.title: Exercise 1: CLI setup and first commands (15 min)
Part A: Install (5 min)
docs.text:
1. Install the CLI with one of these:
npm install -g @github/copilot          # needs Node.js 22+
brew install --cask github-copilot-cli  # macOS
winget install GitHub.Copilot           # Windows
  1. Check the install. Expect a version number.
copilot --version
  1. Sign in if needed. This starts an OAuth device flow in the browser.
copilot
/login
  1. Start copilot and check that the interactive prompt appears. Type /exit to leave.
Problem Fix copilot: command not found Check Node.js 22+, or run npx @github/copilot Authentication fails Run /login, or set GH_TOKEN "Copilot isn't enabled" Check github.com/settings/copilot Permission denied on global npm install Use nvm, or sudo on Linux/macOS

docs.title: Part B: Explain commands (5 min)
docs.text:
Open lab/starter/explain-challenges.md. For each of its five commands:

  1. In copilot, ask: "Explain what this command does: <command>".
  2. Rate the explanation from 1 to 5 for accuracy and edge cases.
  3. Note what it missed or got wrong.
# Command What to look for 1 ls -la Does it explain each flag? 2 find . -name "*.log" -mtime +7 -delete Does it warn about deletion? 3 git log --oneline --graph --all --decorate Does it explain each flag's visual effect? 4 tar czf backup.tar.gz --exclude='node_modules' --exclude='.git' ./src Does it explain compression and exclusions? 5 awk -F',' '{sum[$1]+=$3; count[$1]++} END {for (k in sum) print k, sum[k]/count[k]}' Does it explain the associative arrays and the math?

Compare your notes with lab/solution/explain-answers.md.

docs.title: Part C: Suggest commands (5 min)
docs.text:
Open lab/starter/suggest-challenges.md and choose two tasks. For each:

  1. Describe the task in the CLI, for example "Give me a command to find all Python files larger than 1MB."
  2. Check that the command does what you asked. Run it, or note what it would do.
  3. If it's off, refine the description and retry.
# Task What to look for 1 Find all Python files larger than 1MB find with -size 2 Show commits from the last 7 days by a specific author --since and --author 3 Create a branch, commit, and push in one line Correctly chained commands 4 Find the 10 largest files in the current tree du, or find + sort 5 List open issues assigned to you in a repo gh issue list --assignee

Compare with lab/solution/suggest-answers.md.

docs.title: Checkpoint 1
docs.text:
• copilot --version works and you can start an interactive session
  • You explained five commands and know where Copilot is weak
  • You generated and checked commands for two tasks

docs.title: Exercise 2: Plan, revise, and repair (40 min)
docs.text: Fix bugs, add tests, and refactor in the terminal. Keep the IDE closed.

docs.title: Setup
docs.text:
1. From the curriculum root, copy the starter to a fresh folder:
mkdir -p ~/copilot-labs/session-m2-01
cp -R sessions/session-m2-01-copilot-cli/lab/starter/agent-tasks \
  ~/copilot-labs/session-m2-01/agent-tasks
cp sessions/session-m2-01-copilot-cli/lab/starter/workflow-record.md \
  ~/copilot-labs/session-m2-01/workflow-record.md
cd ~/copilot-labs/session-m2-01/agent-tasks
git init
printf 'node_modules/\nproject-report.md\ncommits.jsonl\n' > .gitignore
git add .gitignore package.json src tests task-list.md
git commit -m "Record training baseline"

Use a new destination if the folder exists. Record plans and fleet results in workflow-record.md.

  1. Install and run the tests. Expect failures: the project has three intentional bugs.
npm install
npm test
  1. The project layout:
agent-tasks/
├── package.json          # Project config with test script
├── src/
│   ├── app.js            # Express app with 3 bugs
│   └── utils.js          # Utility functions needing refactoring
├── tests/
│   └── app.test.js       # Basic tests (some failing due to bugs)
└── task-list.md          # Your 3 tasks for agent mode
  1. Read task-list.md.

docs.title: Task 1: Plan and fix the bugs (15 min)
docs.text:
Start copilot in the project and inspect the controls:

/rename Session M2-01 takeover
/permissions show
/sandbox status
/sandbox policy
/sandbox policy node --version
/limits

Note the permission mode and the filesystem and network restrictions. Approval decides whether a tool may run. The sandbox limits what a process can reach. Don't disable the sandbox or broaden permissions to finish the lab. If the sandbox is unavailable, stop and fix the setup.

In /limits, read the value, unit, minimum, and scope. Set a soft AI-credit limit with the trainer's value, in the dialog or with:

/limits set max-ai-credits <trainer-agreed-value>

The limit is soft. GitHub's command reference describes limits that reset per message, and its session-limit guide describes a cumulative limit. Note what your installed version shows. If the scope is unclear, ask the trainer before you start the next step.

Start in Plan mode:

/plan Read src/app.js and tests/app.test.js. Explain the three failing behaviors.
Plan the smallest fixes. Map each behavior to a target file and an existing test.
Do not edit project files, add dependencies, or refactor unrelated code.

Read the plan, then add a constraint:

Revise the plan so the fixes preserve the existing response fields and status
codes. Explain which steps change and which stay the same.

Before you approve, get a critique:

/rubber-duck Critique the revised repair plan against src/app.js and its tests.
Look for a change that could hide a defect or break the response contract.
Do not edit files.

Rubber duck is a built-in, read-only critic. Copilot picks a contrasting model when one is available. Check each finding against the source. Revise the plan for findings that hold up, and explain the ones you reject. If it finds nothing, note that.

Open /subagents, select rubber duck, and look at Proactive invocation. Leave it as it is. The opt-in persists across sessions and adds model usage.

Save both plans and the critique in workflow-record.md, and name one assumption you challenged. Reject steps that change the public API or test away a defect. Run git diff. Planning shouldn't have changed any file.

Approve the revised plan, leave Plan mode, and ask Copilot to implement it. Then check:

git diff -- src/app.js tests/app.test.js
npm test

Note the test result and any deviation from the plan.

Plan mode isn't a sandbox. Keep tool permissions in place, especially for external and MCP tools. Writing "plan first" in a normal prompt isn't Plan mode.

docs.title: Task 2: Add missing tests (10 min)
docs.text:
In the same session or a new one:

The utils.js file has 4 exported functions but no tests. Create a full test file at
tests/utils.test.js that covers every function, including edge cases. Run the tests
to verify they pass.

Watch for:

  • reading utils.js before writing tests;
  • edge cases (empty strings, negative numbers, null);
  • running the tests on its own;
  • at least three tests per function.
npm test

Expect a new tests/utils.test.js with passing tests for every utility function.

docs.title: Task 3: Refactor from an accepted plan (15 min)
docs.text:
/plan Refactor src/utils.js:
1. Add input validation to all functions (throw TypeError for invalid arguments)
2. Add JSDoc comments to every function
3. Update the tests to cover the new validation behavior (expect throws for bad input)
4. Make sure all tests still pass
Name the files and checks for each step. Do not implement yet.

Approve only the listed behavior changes. Continue in Standard mode and read the diff. Autopilot suits a narrow task, but it doesn't replace permissions or review.

Run npm test. The utilities now validate input and have JSDoc, and all tests pass. Type /exit, then compare your result with lab/solution/agent-tasks/.

Problem Fix Agent doesn't run tests Prompt: "Run npm test to verify" Agent edits the wrong files Stop, read the diff, use /rewind only for edits it can restore Agent loops Press Esc, then give clearer instructions "Permission denied" on a tool Read the requested action and the policy; stop if the lab would need a prohibited action

docs.title: Checkpoint 2
docs.text:
• All three original bugs are fixed
  • The first plan, a challenged assumption, and the revised plan are recorded
  • You checked the diff before approval and after implementation
  • tests/utils.test.js covers every exported function
  • Utilities have validation and JSDoc
  • npm test shows 0 failures

docs.title: Exercise 3: Programmatic output and fleet (35 min)
docs.text: Automate a report in the terminal, then delegate independent analysis of the same project. The app also supports /fleet and /research.

docs.title: Part A: Programmatic mode (15 min)
docs.text:
-p runs one prompt and exits, so you can use it in scripts and pipelines.

  1. Copy the script into your project:
cp sessions/session-m2-01-copilot-cli/lab/starter/cli-exclusive/pipeline-script.sh \
  ~/copilot-labs/session-m2-01/agent-tasks/pipeline-script.sh
cd ~/copilot-labs/session-m2-01/agent-tasks

  1. Open pipeline-script.sh. You fill in the Copilot commands at its TODO comments.

  2. Try a one-shot answer first:

copilot -p "What is the current git branch?" --allow-tool='shell(git)' --silent

Compare it with git branch --show-current. --silent removes CLI commentary. It doesn't fix the answer format.

  1. Try structured output:
copilot -p "Summarize the last 5 commits. Do not edit files." \
  --allow-tool='shell(git log)' --output-format=json > commits.jsonl
copilot_status=$?
printf 'Copilot exit status: %s\n' "$copilot_status"
if [ "$copilot_status" -ne 0 ]; then
  echo "Stop: inspect the Copilot error before parsing output."
else
  node -e 'const fs = require("node:fs"); const lines = fs.readFileSync("commits.jsonl", "utf8").trim().split("\n"); lines.forEach(line => JSON.parse(line)); console.log(`Parsed ${lines.length} JSONL records`);'
fi

--output-format=json emits a JSONL event stream, not one JSON array with the answer. Look at the event types and any error. Parsing every line proves the format, not that the task succeeded. Read the exit status right after the Copilot command.

  1. Complete the TODO sections, by hand or with the CLI:
Read starter/cli-exclusive/pipeline-script.sh and fill in all the TODO sections
  1. Run it:
chmod +x pipeline-script.sh
./pipeline-script.sh

Expect an agent-tasks health report with git history analysis, a code assessment, and a TODO scan. Compare with lab/solution/cli-exclusive/pipeline-script.sh.

Queue a follow-up and background a command. Use a harmless timed command to practice the controls. In interactive Copilot:

Run only node -e "setTimeout(() => console.log('training wait complete'), 15000)"
and report its exit status. Do not edit files or detach the process.

While it runs, type After the command finishes, restate its output and exit status without running it again. and press Ctrl+Q to queue it. Check the pending label, then press Ctrl+X, b to move the running command to the background. Open /tasks to see its state and result.

When the queued follow-up arrives, compare its claim with the real output. If the command finishes before you press the shortcuts, retry once. Backgrounding keeps the work in the CLI session. It doesn't detach the process or make shared-file writes safe. Ctrl+S stashes or restores an unsent draft. It doesn't queue or send it. Note which control did what.

docs.title: Part B: Research with /research (5 min)
docs.text:
/research starts an agent that searches your code, GitHub repositories, and the web, then writes a report.

  1. Pick one topic from starter/cli-exclusive/research-topics.md.
  2. Run it in copilot:
/research What are the security best practices for Express.js middleware in 2026? Cover OWASP Top 10 mitigations.
  1. Watch for: GitHub repository searches, cited sources, time versus a normal prompt, and depth.
  2. Save the output with /share file research.
  3. Compare it with the answer to "tell me about Express.js security."

docs.title: Part C: Plan and supervise a fleet (15 min)
docs.text:
Open starter/cli-exclusive/delegation-scenario.md. Treat the repaired project as a shared snapshot for independent read-only analysis.

  1. Use /plan to split the analysis into independent questions. Give each task input paths, an expected result, and a stop rule. Keep implementation and its dependent tests out of the parallel work.
  2. Accept the breakdown, leave Plan mode, and run:
/fleet Use the accepted analysis plan. Delegate independent read-only tasks:
inspect the route behavior in src/app.js, the input contract in src/utils.js,
and gaps in tests/. Each task must cite files and distinguish a proven defect
from a proposed improvement. Do not edit files, install packages, or use the
network. Stop on scope growth or the agreed usage limit.
  1. Run /tasks and open the task details. Stop any task that starts editing or widens its scope.
  2. Check at least one claim from each result against the source or a focused test. Reject claims you can't support.
  3. Ask the parent to reconcile duplicates or disagreements. Run /usage and note the usage and whether the coordination was worth it.

You need live child-task results. Copilot decides how many agents to use. If it keeps the analysis sequential, note that and ask the trainer to adjust the split. /delegate is cloud delegation and doesn't count as fleet practice (see M3-02).

Problem Fix /research is slow 1 to 3 minutes is normal /delegate fails Push the repo to a GitHub remote and check cloud agent access /fleet not recognized npm update -g @github/copilot Programmatic mode hangs Add --max-autopilot-continues=5

docs.title: Checkpoint 3
docs.text:
• You ran -p with --silent and --allow-tool
  • pipeline-script.sh runs and produces a report
  • You compared /research with a regular prompt
  • You used /plan, /fleet, and /tasks and read live child results
  • Each accepted child claim has a file reference or focused test
  • You noted usage and whether parallel work helped

docs.title: Exercise 4: Recovery, isolated alternatives, and surface choice (30 min)
Part A: Recover a disposable edit (10 min)
docs.text:
Run npm test and read the repair diff. Commit the reviewed project files, including the lockfile and the finished script. Leave out generated reports and credentials: keep them outside the worktree or in .gitignore, so git status is clean before you fork. The commit makes the repair available to a worktree fork.

Ask Copilot to create only recovery-note.txt containing temporary training note. Check the file and git status. Then run /rewind and compare the two choices:

  • Conversation only removes turns and leaves files.
  • Conversation + files also restores the agent's tracked edits for those turns. Later manual edits may be skipped.

Choose Conversation + files. Check that the note is gone and the committed repair remains. Don't edit the note by hand first. Rewind isn't a Git rollback and can't undo a push or an external action.

docs.title: Part B: Fork context and move a draft (10 min)
docs.text:
From the clean repaired repo:

/fork worktree

Ask the fork for pwd, its branch, and git worktree list, and compare them with the parent. A plain /fork copies conversation context only, without isolating files. /fork worktree adds a separate checkout of HEAD. The parent's uncommitted work stays behind.

In the fork, ask for a read-only alternative to the utility refactor, then have Copilot write only alternative-note.txt with it. Check the file and run:

/move

Check the new path and Git status. The draft should now be in the new worktree. If the client reports a conflict, don't force the move. Go back to the parent with /resume and check its path, branch, and status. Don't merge the alternative or delete worktrees yet.

/worktree leaves uncommitted edits behind. /move carries them. /resume restores a conversation, /compact summarizes one, and /new starts fresh. Check the workspace after each step.

docs.title: Part C: Surface comparison and cheat sheet (10 min)
docs.text:
Pick one task from lab/starter/comparison-tasks.md. Do it in the CLI and the IDE, and note the tradeoff. Pick two scenarios from lab/starter/workflow-scenarios.md and explain your surface choice.

Fill in lab/starter/cli-cheatsheet-template.md with your top five CLI commands, your CLI-versus-IDE rules, your shortcuts and aliases, and notes from today. lab/solution/cli-cheatsheet-example.md shows a finished one.

Restore your original /limits setting. Keep any cap that existed before the lab.

docs.title: Checkpoint 4
docs.text:
• You did the same task in the CLI and IDE and noted the tradeoffs
  • The rewind removed the note and kept the committed repair
  • You checked the worktree fork and moved draft against real paths and Git status
  • You chose CLI or IDE for two scenarios
  • You have a CLI workflow cheat sheet

docs.title: Final deliverable
docs.text:
Submit one folder with:

  1. The fixed agent-tasks/ project and passing npm test output.
  2. The finished pipeline-script.sh and one generated health report.
  3. workflow-record.md with the critique, controls, queue and background results, recovery and worktree state, and fleet results.
  4. The CLI-versus-IDE comparison and your cheat sheet.

Another learner should be able to trace the plan revision to the diff, check the accepted fleet findings, and run the tests and script. Shell-only work or a cloud delegation doesn't complete this lab.

Demonstrate the standalone CLI in terminal workflows and show when it beats an IDE. Use lab/starter/agent-tasks/ for the demos.

docs.title: Before delivery
docs.text:
• Install the CLI (npm install -g @github/copilot, Node.js 22+) and run /login.
  • Set the terminal font to 24pt or larger.
  • Rehearse every demo. CLI versions change quickly.
  • Check /plan, /fleet, /tasks, /usage, /rubber-duck, /subagents, /rewind, /fork worktree, /move, /resume, and /limits in the installed version, including the limit's units, minimum, scope, and reset behavior.
  • Check the permission mode and sandbox policy. Don't weaken them.
  • Agree a usage limit and practice stopping a child task.
  • Rehearse Ctrl+Q and Ctrl+X, b with the lab's 15-second command.

docs.title: Section 1: Why a dedicated CLI session? (5 min)
docs.text:
"You've used Copilot in VS Code through Chat, inline suggestions, and agent mode. The CLI is a separate surface with its own agent loop."

It has its own agent loop. The copilot binary reads and writes files, runs shell commands, manages Git, talks to GitHub.com, and orchestrates subagents.

It has terminal-oriented features:

  • Autopilot mode for autonomous continuation (tool permissions still apply)
  • Programmatic mode (-p) for scripting
  • Custom model providers (Ollama, Azure OpenAI, Anthropic)
  • Built-in specialized agents (check the installed version for the list)
  • Parallel subagents with /fleet, cloud delegation with /delegate
  • Hooks for CI/CD automation
  • OpenTelemetry monitoring

It works where IDEs don't: SSH sessions, CI/CD scripts, headless containers, and machines where you can't install VS Code.

docs.title: Section 2: Installation and setup (5 min)
docs.text:
The CLI is a standalone binary, not a gh extension.

Method Command Platform npm npm install -g @github/copilot All (Node.js 22+) Homebrew brew install --cask github-copilot-cli macOS WinGet winget install GitHub.Copilot Windows Install script curl -fsSL https://gh.io/copilot-install \| bash macOS, Linux

Authentication: /login on first launch starts an OAuth device flow. In CI/CD, set COPILOT_GITHUB_TOKEN or GH_TOKEN.

copilot
# Ask: "What files are in the current directory?"
/exit

If learners already have it installed, skip to the interactive interface.

docs.title: Section 3: Core interactive modes (10 min)
docs.text:
Shift+Tab cycles three modes:

Mode Behavior Use it when Standard Copilot responds and asks permission before acting Default for most work Plan Copilot analyzes, asks questions, and builds a plan before writing code You want to review the approach first Autopilot Copilot works without asking at each step The task is narrow and you know what you want

Autopilot can continue without another prompt, but tool permissions still apply. Keep the task small and read the result.

Required lab practice: run /plan, challenge one assumption, and request a /rubber-duck critique before approving. Check findings against the source, then revise or explain what you rejected. Check the diff before approval and after implementation.

Rubber duck is a built-in, read-only critic. Copilot picks a contrasting model when one is available. Check /subagents Proactive invocation and leave it unchanged. The opt-in persists and adds model usage.

Plan mode protects project edits during planning. It isn't a sandbox for external or MCP tools, so keep those permissions restricted. A normal "plan first" prompt isn't Plan mode.

docs.title: Slash commands
docs.text:
The CLI has 40+ slash commands. The ones this session uses:

  • Session: /clear or /new, /resume, /compact, /context, /usage
  • Agents: /agent, /delegate (cloud agent), /fleet (parallel subagents), /plan, /research, /review, /security-review (practiced in M2-04), /pr, /diff
  • Configuration: /model, /mcp, /skills, /init (generates copilot-instructions.md)

The app also provides /plan, /fleet, and /review.

docs.title: Demo: interactive modes
docs.text:
copilot
# Standard: "What does this project do?"

/plan Explain the failing behaviors in src/app.js. Name the files and tests for the smallest fixes. Do not implement.

# Challenge it: "Preserve response fields and status codes. Revise the affected steps."
# Check git diff, then approve implementation

Show where learners save both plan versions in workflow-record.md.

docs.title: Section 4: Programmatic mode (10 min)
docs.text:
-p runs one prompt and exits. Use it in scripts, CI/CD, and cron.

copilot -p "PROMPT" [OPTIONS]
Flag What it does -p "PROMPT" Single-shot prompt, exit when done --allow-tool='shell(git log)' Pre-approve that operation; other permissions still apply --deny-tool='shell(rm)' Block specific tools --output-format=json JSONL output for machine parsing -s / --silent Output only the agent's response --share=PATH Export session to Markdown --autopilot Enable autonomous continuation --max-autopilot-continues=10 Cap autonomous iterations --no-ask-user Disable all user prompts (fully headless)

Changelog from git history:

copilot -p "Generate a changelog from the last 10 commits" \
  --allow-tool='shell(git)' --silent > CHANGELOG.md

Review a diff in CI:

copilot -p "Summarize the current diff. Do not edit files." \
  --allow-tool='shell(git diff)' --output-format=json > review-events.jsonl

Check the exit status before parsing. A JSON parser accepting the file doesn't mean the task succeeded. To get the answer, extract it using the event schema of the installed version, then validate it. Don't assume every event has a .content field.

Infrastructure validation:

copilot -p "Check this Terraform for security issues and fix them" \
  --allow-tool='view' --allow-tool='edit' --allow-tool='shell(terraform)' \
  --autopilot

For refactoring, use the lab's /plan flow to review scope before edits. Don't remove permission prompts to finish a demo.

docs.title: Fine-grained tool permissions
docs.text:
Kind(argument) syntax restricts individual operations:

# Allow all git commands except push
copilot --allow-tool='shell(git:*)' --deny-tool='shell(git push)'

# Allow specific MCP tools
copilot --allow-tool='MyMCP(create_issue)'

# Block reading sensitive files
copilot --deny-tool='read(.env)' --deny-tool='read(**/secrets/*)'

# Only allow read operations (safe for CI analysis)
copilot --available-tools='view,grep,glob'

docs.title: Demo
docs.text:
copilot -p "Explain what 'git rebase -i HEAD~3' does" --silent

copilot -p "Create a Python script that reads a CSV and outputs summary statistics" \
  --allow-tool='create' --silent

copilot -p "List all TODO comments in this project" \
  --allow-tool='shell(grep)' --silent | sort | uniq -c | sort -rn

docs.title: Section 5: Built-in agents and subagents (10 min)
docs.text:
Check /agent for the installed agents.

Agent Purpose Explore Fast codebase exploration and Q&A Task Commands such as tests, builds, and lints Code Review High signal-to-noise review of diffs for bugs, security, and logic Security Review Read-only review of current changes for exploitable vulnerabilities Rubber Duck Adversarial feedback on designs and answers

Plan is a mode, not a custom agent. /plan prepares an implementation plan.

The main agent delegates to specialists in separate context windows. For a complex task it might explore first, then run tests with the task agent. Available concurrency depends on plan and configuration.

/delegate sends work to the Copilot cloud agent. It creates a branch, writes code, and opens a draft PR:

/delegate Create a PR that fixes issue #42

Cloud delegation is practiced in M3-02. It doesn't replace the local fleet run.

/fleet delegates independent work:

/fleet Use the accepted analysis plan. Inspect route behavior, utility contracts,
and test gaps as independent read-only tasks. Cite files. Do not edit or use the
network. Stop on scope growth or the agreed usage limit.

Copilot decides how to split the work. Don't promise one agent per bullet or a speedup. Keep shared decisions with the parent and check every accepted claim. The app's /orchestrate skill is taught in M7-05.

/research runs deep research and produces a report. Check its citations.

/research What are the best practices for rate limiting in Express.js?

/tasks monitors background subagents. Open a task's details, stop it if it leaves scope, and finish with /usage.

docs.title: Demo
docs.text:
copilot
/fleet Inspect routes, utilities, and test gaps using the accepted plan.
/tasks
/usage

docs.title: Section 6: Terminal automation and session control (10 min)
docs.text:
Show the controls, then the lab's recovery flow. The providers, hooks, ACP, and telemetry material below is reference, not part of the hour.

/permissions show
/sandbox status
/sandbox policy node --version
/limits

Tool approval and the sandbox are different. Approval decides whether a tool runs. The sandbox limits filesystem and network access. Don't disable the sandbox or change the permission mode to remove a denial.

Record the original /limits value, then set a trainer-agreed soft AI-credit limit. Restore the original afterward. GitHub's command reference describes per-response limits, and its session-limit guide describes a cumulative cap. Check what the installed UI shows. If the scope is unclear, stop before the metered task.

Show the 15-second command from the lab. Queue a follow-up with Ctrl+Q, move the command to the background with Ctrl+X, b, and inspect /tasks. Check the real output before trusting the queued follow-up's summary. Ctrl+S stashes a draft without sending it. Backgrounding doesn't detach the process or isolate writes.

For recovery, commit a repair, let the agent create a disposable note, then open /rewind. Conversation-only and conversation-plus-files differ. Rewind doesn't undo external writes or replace Git rollback.

Use /fork worktree to carry context to a new checkout of HEAD. A plain fork shares files. Move only the disposable draft with /move, compare the old and new paths, and return with /resume. Don't merge the alternative.

docs.title: Custom model providers
docs.text:
Provider Setup Ollama (local) copilot --model ollama:deepseek-coder Azure OpenAI Configure via environment variables Anthropic Direct copilot --model anthropic:claude-opus-4

"If policy stops you sending code to GitHub's servers, point the CLI at a local Ollama instance running an open-source model."

docs.title: Hooks
docs.text:
Hooks are external commands that fire at lifecycle points. Configure them in .github/hooks/*.json:

Event When Can block? preToolUse Before each tool executes Yes: allow, deny, or modify postToolUse After a tool completes Yes: can replace the result permissionRequest Before the permission dialog Yes: auto-approve or deny sessionStart Session begins No agentStop Agent finishes a turn Yes: can force continuation + 8 more events Various lifecycle points Various

Uses: SAST scanning before edits are committed, logging tool calls for audit, running tests before git push, linting after every edit, and tool approval in headless CI/CD.

{
  "version": 1,
  "hooks": {
    "preToolUse": [{
      "type": "command",
      "bash": "./scripts/validate-edit.sh",
      "timeoutSec": 30
    }]
  }
}

docs.title: ACP server mode (preview)
docs.text:
The CLI can act as an AI backend for any ACP-compatible tool, such as custom IDE integrations, web interfaces, or automation:

copilot --acp --transport=sse --port=8080

docs.title: OpenTelemetry monitoring
docs.text:
copilot --otel-endpoint=http://localhost:4318

This produces traces, spans, and metrics for tool calls, model requests, and token use. Send them to Grafana, Datadog, or any OTLP-compatible backend. It matters most for enterprise audiences.

docs.title: Session management and remote access
docs.text:
• Resume: copilot --continue
  • Cross-device: start on GitHub.com, continue in the CLI with /resume
  • Remote: /remote opens access from GitHub.com and GitHub Mobile
  • Sharing: /share gist exports the session as a gist

Show /context before a phase change. Use /compact Preserve the accepted plan, changed files, and remaining checks to continue the same thread, and note that a summary can lose detail. Save the accepted plan and test output in the workflow record before starting a fresh session.

docs.title: Section 7: CLI vs IDE decision framework (5 min)
docs.text:
Scenario CLI IDE Chat IDE Agent Copilot App SSH'd into a remote server Yes No No No Scripting and CI/CD automation Yes No No No Quick shell command help Yes No No Check support Custom or local model Check provider support Check editor Check editor Check provider support Deep codebase research Yes Yes Check editor Yes Parallel multi-agent orchestration Yes Check editor Check editor Yes Writing code in an editor No Yes Yes No Visual diff review before accepting /diff Check editor Yes Yes Inline suggestions while typing No No Yes No Multi-file refactoring with visual diffs No No Yes No Quick question about selected code No Yes No Yes Chat-only (no coding) Check support Yes No Yes Shared artifact and direct steering No No Check support Yes
  • CLI: automation, scripting, headless environments, parallel subagents. Fits operators, SREs, and CI/CD.
  • IDE Chat: quick questions and refinements with open-file context.
  • IDE Agent Mode: multi-step coding with visual control. Review diffs before accepting complex edits.
  • Copilot App: isolated developer sessions and review (M2-05), customization and canvas extensions (M3-01), and supervised child sessions with /orchestrate (M7-05).

"Use the IDE for daily coding, the CLI for terminal automation, Chat for short questions, and the App when shared state helps people steer the work."

docs.title: Copilot App orientation
docs.text:
The App is another Copilot surface. M3-01 covers it in depth. In brief:

  • Agent sessions are app-managed.
  • Customize area: plugins, skills, MCP servers, and canvases.
  • Shared canvases: work with an agent on a visible plan, board, or checklist.

docs.title: Cross-IDE comparison
docs.text:
IDE Completions Chat Agent Mode Notes VS Code Yes (GA) Yes (GA) Yes (GA) Primary platform, most features first Visual Studio Yes (GA) Yes (GA) Yes (GA) Full support for .NET developers JetBrains (IntelliJ, PyCharm, WebStorm) Yes (GA) Yes (GA) Yes (GA) Multi-language work Eclipse Yes (GA) Yes (GA) Yes (Preview) Xcode Yes (GA) Yes (GA) Yes (Preview) Apple development Vim / Neovim Yes (GA) No No Completions only Azure Data Studio Yes (GA) Yes (GA) No Database-focused Sublime Text Yes (GA) Yes (GA) No Lightweight

"This curriculum uses VS Code as the baseline IDE. Check the current feature matrix before teaching a different IDE."

docs.title: CLI-native workflow patterns
docs.text:
Ops/SRE:

ssh prod-server
copilot -p "Analyze the last 100 lines of /var/log/app.log and identify errors" \
  --allow-tool='shell(tail,grep,cat)' --silent

CI/CD (in a GitHub Actions step):

copilot -p "Review the diff for this PR" \
  --allow-tool='shell(git)' --output-format=json > review.json

Automation (nightly cron):

copilot -p "Generate a weekly code quality report for src/" \
  --allow-tool='view,grep,glob' --silent > reports/weekly-$(date +%F).md

Data engineering:

copilot -p "Explain the schema in migrations/ and suggest indexes for common queries" \
  --allow-tool='view,grep' --silent

docs.title: Section 8: Wrap-up (5 min)
docs.text:
1. The CLI is a standalone agent.
  2. -p makes Copilot scriptable for CI/CD and automation.
  3. Built-in agents and /fleet run work in parallel.
  4. Custom model providers allow local or private models.
  5. Hooks add security controls and audit.
  6. Pick the CLI or IDE by the task.

"M2-02 covers agent mode in the IDE, with visual diffs and inline changes. The CLI stays the terminal automation surface."

docs.title: Common questions
docs.text:
Do I need both the CLI and the IDE extension? Use the surface that fits the task.

Can I use the CLI in GitHub Actions? Yes. Use programmatic mode with task-specific permissions and the documented authentication. M4-01 covers workflow setup.

Is the CLI safe for production servers? This lab uses a synthetic local project. Production use needs its own permission and data review.

Can I use the CLI without internet? Only with a custom provider pointing at a local model such as Ollama. GitHub-hosted models need a connection.

How does the CLI handle large codebases? /context shows usage. /compact summarizes the thread and can lose detail. Keep the accepted plan and test results in files, and start a fresh session with a handoff when the old conversation stops helping.

Can I share sessions with my team? Yes. /share gist creates a secret gist, and /share file PATH exports Markdown. You can also resume across devices.

Built-in agents and subagents 10 min 40 min 6. Automation and session control 10 min 50 min 7. CLI vs IDE framework 5 min 55 min 8. Wrap-up 5 min 60 min

docs.text: The lab runs 120 minutes: setup 15, plan and repair 40, programmatic and fleet 35, recovery and surface choice 30. Learners pick two command-generation examples and one surface-comparison task. Require workflow-record.md, passing tests, a reviewed diff, and a health report. Each accepted child claim needs a file reference or focused test. The lab requires /fleet. /delegate doesn't replace it.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: Build and extend one Todo API with agent mode in an IDE. Compare Ask and Agent mode on the same feature, then redirect a multi-file change. At each checkpoint, decide whether to accept the work, revise it, or stop.

docs.title: Learning outcomes
docs.text:
• Explain how assistant and agent workflows differ
  • Use agent mode in VS Code for multi-step, multi-file tasks
  • Choose between agent mode, Chat, and inline suggestions
  • Use TODO code actions to hand work to the cloud agent
  • Review plans, diffs, commands, and test output at each checkpoint

docs.title: Session materials
docs.text: Resource Location Lab exercises lab/ Lab starter files lab/starter/ Lab solution files lab/solution/

docs.title: Key topics
docs.text:
• From autocomplete to assistant to agent
  • The agent loop: plan, act, observe, review, revise
  • Tool use: terminal commands, file operations, web search
  • Multi-file changes in agent mode
  • Trust boundaries and when to intervene
  • TODO code actions for cloud agent delegation
  • When to use Chat or Agent mode

docs.title: The agent loop
docs.text:
Plan → Act → Observe → Review → Revise or stop

Use the loop to review the work.

docs.title: Task contract
docs.text:
## Goal
Add one small, testable behavior.

## Constraints
- Named files and data only
- Required tests
- No new dependencies

## Done
- Tests pass
- A human accepts the change

docs.title: Review checkpoints
docs.text:
• Read the proposed file changes.
  • Read every command before it runs.
  • Check test results and side effects.
  • Stop when scope, data, or the stop rule is unclear.

docs.title: Agenda
docs.text: Time Topic 0:00 Assistant-to-agent shift 0:08 Agent loop and tools 0:18 Task contracts and trust 0:28 Multi-file live demo 0:43 Chat vs. agent mode 0:50 Redirect and stop 0:57 Lab handoff

docs.title: From autocomplete to agent
docs.text:
Mode Developer supplies Surface returns Inline Local code context A continuation Chat A question and references Guidance or a proposed edit Agent Goal, constraints, and repository A multi-step change with a diff and check results

More autonomy needs clear file limits, progress checks, and review.

docs.title: What agent mode can do
docs.text:
• inspect repository files and conventions;
  • plan a sequence of changes;
  • edit multiple related files;
  • run terminal commands and tests;
  • observe failures and revise;
  • use tools, including configured MCP tools.

docs.title: One loop, many checkpoints
docs.text:
Goal and constraints
        ↓
Plan ──→ Act ──→ Observe
 ↑                   │
 └──── revise ───────┘
        ↓
Human review or stop

docs.title: Tool use and trust
docs.text: Tool action Review question Read a file Do you need this path and its data? Edit a file Does the task require it? Run a command Is it understood, reversible, and scoped? Add a dependency Is it necessary? Search the web Can repository context leave your environment? Call an MCP tool Which server, and what can it do?

docs.title: Multi-file work is a graph
docs.text:
route.ts ──calls──→ service.ts
   │                    │
   └──verified by──→ route.test.ts
                        │
                  documents behavior
                        ↓
                     README.md

Name the behavior you want to change. Review every changed file and check that its callers and tests still fit.

docs.title: Demo brief: one feature, three files
docs.text:
Add `completed` filtering to the task list endpoint.

Acceptance criteria:
- `GET /tasks?completed=true` returns completed tasks only.
- Invalid values return HTTP 400.
- Existing behavior without the parameter is unchanged.
- Focused tests cover true, false, and invalid values.

Constraints: no new dependencies; edit route, service, and tests only.

docs.title: Concrete demo code
docs.text:
const value = req.query.completed;
if (value !== undefined && value !== "true" && value !== "false") {
  return res.status(400).json({ error: "completed must be true or false" });
}

const completed = value === undefined ? undefined : value === "true";
return res.json(taskService.list({ completed }));

Ask the agent to implement and test the smallest valid change, then explain it.

docs.title: Narrate the demo
docs.text:
1. Show a clean working tree and the focused test command.
  2. Paste the task contract and request a plan before edits.
  3. Check that the plan names route, service, and tests.
  4. Approve only commands needed for the task.
  5. When a test fails, ask the agent to explain before revising.
  6. Read the final diff and run tests yourself.

docs.title: Intervene, redirect, stop
docs.text:
Use a correction that preserves the original contract:

Stop. Do not change the response schema or add dependencies.
Keep the existing service API and add only the optional filter.
Show the revised plan before editing.

Stop for unexpected file scope, destructive commands, sensitive data, unexpected network access, or repeated changes with no new test results.

docs.title: Same task: Chat or agent mode?
docs.text:
Use Chat when… Use agent mode when… You need explanation or options The outcome spans related files You want one surgical edit Tests can drive iteration Requirements are still forming Requirements and constraints are clear You need to retain manual control Tool output helps you check the work

Work manually when risk or ambiguity makes an agent a poor fit.

docs.title: TODO code actions
docs.text:
A TODO can define a short task to delegate:

// TODO: reject duplicate task titles within the same project.

Before delegating:

  • convert the comment into acceptance criteria;
  • check the target repository and branch;
  • remove sensitive context;
  • define the tests.

docs.title: Demo debrief
docs.text:
• Which plan step gave the earliest useful signal?
  • Which command needed the most scrutiny?
  • Did the agent touch exactly the expected files?
  • Would Chat have been faster for this task?

docs.title: Lab handoff
docs.text:
Build one Todo API, add ownership and due dates, then redirect a repository refactor. Along the way you will:

  1. watch tool calls and multi-file edits;
  2. redirect the agent after a scope change;
  3. compare Ask and Agent mode;
  4. try a TODO delegation if your account supports it.

Final deliverable: The tested API, plan, comparison, course correction, and your accept, revise, or stop decision.

docs.title: Remember
docs.text:
1. Agent mode fits defined, testable, multi-step work.
  2. Write the task limits before the agent starts.
  3. Tool approval and file scope are trust decisions.
  4. Redirect or stop the agent when needed.
  5. You decide whether to accept the work.

docs.title: Lab overview
docs.text:
You build one Todo API throughout the lab. Scaffold it from a brief, compare Ask and Agent mode on the same feature, and redirect the agent when the requirement changes. Finish with an accept, revise, or stop decision.

Stage Work Time 1 Prepare and scaffold the Todo API 30 min 2 Compare Ask and Agent mode on one feature 35 min 3 Redirect a multi-file change 35 min 4 Review the diff and test results, then finish the handoff 20 min

docs.title: Before you start
docs.text:
You need VS Code with GitHub Copilot Agent mode, Node.js and npm, and a disposable workspace. Use synthetic data only. Manual editing skips the practice this lab is for: planning, tool approval, steering, and review.

Create a workspace outside the curriculum folder:

mkdir -p ~/copilot-labs/session-m2-02
cp sessions/session-m2-02-agent-mode-ide/lab/starter/project-brief.md \
  ~/copilot-labs/session-m2-02/
cp sessions/session-m2-02-agent-mode-ide/lab/starter/feature-spec.md \
  ~/copilot-labs/session-m2-02/
cp sessions/session-m2-02-agent-mode-ide/lab/starter/course-correction.md \
  ~/copilot-labs/session-m2-02/
cd ~/copilot-labs/session-m2-02

Create lab-notes.md with these headings:

# Session M2-02 Lab Notes

## Task contract
## Agent plan
## Tool and file review
## Ask versus Agent comparison
## Course correction
## Final decision

docs.title: Stage 1: Prepare and scaffold the Todo API (30 minutes)
Write the task contract
docs.text:
Read project-brief.md, then add a short contract to lab-notes.md:

Goal: Build the Todo API described in project-brief.md.
Allowed scope: The session-m2-02 workspace only.
Commands: npm install, npm test, and npm start.
Non-goals: No database, front end, deployment, or extra dependencies.
Completion: Required routes exist and the test suite passes.
Stop: Pause on network access beyond npm, destructive commands, or work outside scope.

docs.title: Ask Agent mode to plan first
docs.text:
Open the workspace in VS Code and select Agent mode:

Read project-brief.md. Before editing, return a plan with the files you expect to
create, the commands you need, the tests that prove completion, and any decision
that is missing. Do not edit files yet.

Reject extra features and unexplained dependencies.

docs.title: Scaffold the project
docs.text:
Create the Todo API in a todo-api directory. Stay within the approved plan. Pause
before installing packages. After approval, implement the project and run its tests.

At each pause:

  1. Check the command and working directory.
  2. Check that the action supports the brief.
  3. Read the changed files before the next command.
  4. Note any revision in lab-notes.md.

Then run the tests yourself:

cd todo-api
npm test

If the project has no working test script, have the agent add one covering create, list, validation, update, and not-found behavior.

Compare your project with lab/solution/todo-api/. It's an example, not a file-for-file requirement.

docs.title: Checkpoint 1
docs.text:
• The project lives in todo-api/ with the routes from project-brief.md.
  • The agent stayed inside the workspace.
  • You reviewed package changes before installation.
  • npm test passes.
  • lab-notes.md has the accepted plan and any corrections.

docs.title: Stage 2: Compare Ask and Agent mode on one feature (35 minutes)
docs.text: feature-spec.md adds ownership and due-date behavior to the same API.

docs.title: Ask mode
docs.text:
Keep the passing baseline:

cp -R todo-api todo-api-ask

Open todo-api-ask/, switch to Ask mode, and ask:

Read feature-spec.md and explain the exact code and tests needed to add this feature
to todo-api. Give changes file by file. Do not assume files that are not present.

Apply enough of the answer to test the workflow. Track messages sent, manual edits, copy and paste operations, commands you ran, and missing context or wrong assumptions. Stop after 12 minutes and save the result or diff. Keep the original todo-api/ as the clean baseline for Agent mode.

docs.title: Agent mode
docs.text:
Read feature-spec.md and inspect todo-api. Propose the smallest multi-file plan that
implements the feature without changing existing behavior. Include focused tests.
Wait for approval before editing.

Approve only the work the plan describes, and watch each file and command. Then:

cd todo-api
npm test

Add this table to lab-notes.md:

What you observed Ask mode Agent mode Prompts or messages Manual edits Files changed Commands run Corrections needed Final test result

docs.title: Checkpoint 2
docs.text:
• Existing tests still pass.
  • New tests cover owner and due-date behavior.
  • The implementation follows the existing project structure.
  • The table uses counts or examples you observed.
  • You can say why Agent mode did or didn't help.

docs.title: Stage 3: Redirect a multi-file change (35 minutes)
docs.text: Open course-correction.md, but don't give it to the agent yet.

docs.title: Start the original task
docs.text:
Refactor todo-api so route handlers delegate storage operations to a small repository
module. Keep the HTTP contract unchanged. Add or update tests, and stop after the
repository module and first route integration are complete.

Check the first stage:

  • Did it preserve current behavior?
  • Is the module boundary clear?
  • Did it avoid unrelated formatting or dependency changes?
  • Do the focused tests pass?

docs.title: Apply the course correction
docs.text:
Read course-correction.md and redirect the active task:

Pause. Apply the new constraints in course-correction.md. Revise the plan before
editing. Keep completed work only when it still fits the new requirement.

Reject any plan that rewrites the project without need. The agent should adjust the repository boundary, validation, and tests while keeping the API intact.

cd todo-api
npm test

If the agent asks for an unexpected dependency, network access, or a wider file scope, stop. Note the unfinished work and make the smallest safe change by hand.

docs.title: Checkpoint 3
docs.text:
• course-correction.md changed the plan before more edits.
  • The final diff stays inside todo-api/.
  • The API contract is still compatible.
  • Tests cover the changed behavior.
  • lab-notes.md says whether you accepted, revised, or stopped, and why.

docs.title: Stage 4: Review the diff and finish the handoff (20 minutes)
docs.text:
Review the project as if another engineer submitted it.

  1. Read git diff --stat and git diff, or use the editor's change view.
  2. Check that each changed file serves a requirement in the brief, feature spec, or course correction.
  3. Run npm test again.
  4. Start the service and make one create request and one filtered list request.
  5. Write the final decision: accept, revise, or stop.
curl -X POST http://localhost:3000/api/todos \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"title":"Review agent work","owner":"learner","dueDate":"2026-10-15"}'

curl "http://localhost:3000/api/todos?owner=learner"

Don't approve the work because the agent says it succeeded. Use the diff, tests, and API behavior. lab/solution/final-review.md is the trainer's reference.

docs.title: Checkpoint 4
docs.text:
• The final diff matches the scope you accepted.
  • Package changes are explained.
  • Test output is saved in lab-notes.md.
  • The manual API check matches the feature spec.
  • The final decision names remaining risk.

docs.title: Final deliverable
docs.text:
Submit the session-m2-02 workspace with:

  1. The completed todo-api/ project.
  2. Passing test output and two manual API checks.
  3. lab-notes.md with the contract, plan, tool and file review, comparison, course correction, and final decision.
  4. A note on any action you stopped or rejected.

A reviewer should be able to trace the final code to your plan, see where you redirected the agent, and reproduce the checks.

docs.title: Trainer Guide
docs.text: Overview Lab Trainer Guide

docs.title: Session M2-02: IDE agent workflows
docs.text: 00:00 Start timer Reset timer Print guide      Enable timer shortcut (T)

docs.title: Before teaching
docs.text:
• Pick a training repository with a small task and clear acceptance criteria.
  • Check that Agent mode works in your editor.
  • Use synthetic data only.

docs.title: Session objective
docs.text:
Show learners how to review work at each step of the agent loop.

Plan → Act → Observe → Review → Revise or stop

Learners define the task and approve actions. The agent proposes work inside those limits.

docs.title: One-hour plan
docs.text:
Time Segment Result 0:00 to 0:08 Assistant-to-agent shift Learners tell a continuation, an answer, and a goal-driven task apart 0:08 to 0:18 Agent loop and tools The group knows what to check at each stage 0:18 to 0:28 Task contracts and trust The contract and stop rules are visible 0:28 to 0:43 Multi-file demo The group reviews the plan, commands, diff, and test output 0:43 to 0:50 Chat, agent, or manual Learners pick a workflow from the task 0:50 to 0:57 Redirect and stop Learners redirect or stop without widening scope 0:57 to 1:00 Close and lab handoff

If time runs short, use the prepared plan instead of waiting for a generated one, stop the demo after the route and test review, and run one redirect instead of two. Never cut the independent test run or the stop rules.

docs.title: Segment 1: From assistant to agent (0:00 to 0:08)
docs.text:
1. Inline assistance proposes a local continuation.
  2. Chat usually answers or proposes a small edit.
  3. An agent can pursue a goal through several actions.
  4. More actions need more review. You stay accountable.

Present three fictional tasks:

  • explain one regular expression;
  • change one error message;
  • add an optional filter across route, service, and tests.

Ask learners to choose Chat, a manual edit, or an agent workflow, and say how much review it needs.

"At each step, you need output you can check before the agent continues."

docs.title: Segment 2: Plan, act, observe, review (0:08 to 0:18)
docs.text:
• Plan: map acceptance criteria to files, commands, and risks.
  • Act: approve only the read, edit, or command the task needs.
  • Observe: read command output and changed files.
  • Review: compare behavior and scope with the contract.
  • Revise: change one assumption at a time and check the new result.
  • Stop: end the task when scope, data, permissions, or repeated failures cross a limit.

After each stage, ask:

  • Plan: Does every step support an acceptance criterion?
  • Act: Was this file or command necessary?
  • Observe: What changed, and what does the output show?
  • Review: Would a reviewer accept this?

docs.title: Segment 3: Task contract and trust (0:18 to 0:28)
docs.text:
Open the starter task and write this contract:

Goal: add optional completed filtering to a fictional task list.

Acceptance criteria:
- completed=true returns only completed tasks.
- completed=false returns only incomplete tasks.
- another value produces the existing HTTP 400 error shape.
- omitting completed preserves current behavior.

Constraints:
- route, service, and focused tests only.
- no dependency, network access, or response-schema change.
- show a plan before editing.

Done:
- focused tests pass independently.
- final diff stays in scope.
- a human reviewer accepts the result.
Proposed action Question before approval Read a file Do you need this path and its data? Edit a file Which criterion requires the edit? Run a test Do you understand the command and its scope? Add a package Is it necessary? Use the network or an external tool Where does the data go?

"We'll direct one feature and pause at each checkpoint."

docs.title: Demo: optional task filter (0:28 to 0:43)
docs.text:
Use a disposable fictional TypeScript project or prepared excerpts. Start from a clean working tree. Show the focused test command without running it yet. Don't install packages or connect to external systems.

route.ts → task-service.ts
    └────→ route.test.ts

Opening prompt:

Implement the attached completed-filter task contract.
First inspect only the route, service, and focused test.
Return a three-step plan before editing.
Do not add dependencies, use the network, or change the response schema.
Stop if existing behavior is ambiguous.

The plan should:

  1. inspect query parsing and the existing error shape;
  2. pass an optional boolean to the service and filter without changing the unfiltered path;
  3. add true, false, invalid, and omitted-parameter tests.

Steps:

  1. Compare the plan with the contract. Reject steps that touch other files or add dependencies.
  2. Approve only reads in the named scope.
  3. If your surface can, ask for the proposed diff before broad commands.
  4. Check parsing for exact "true" and "false".
  5. Check that undefined keeps the existing service behavior.
  6. Check tests for all four criteria.
  7. Run the focused test command yourself.
  8. Read git diff --stat and the full diff, and look for response-schema or dependency changes.
  9. Decide: accept, revise, or stop.

Expected code shape (an example, not a required pattern):

const value = req.query.completed;
if (value !== undefined && value !== "true" && value !== "false") {
  return res.status(400).json({ error: "completed must be true or false" });
}
const completed = value === undefined ? undefined : value === "true";
return res.json(taskService.list({ completed }));

Expected result: four focused cases, correct filtering, the stated 400 shape, an unchanged unfiltered list, only three files changed, and no package or external access.

Ask learners:

  • Which test covers the omitted parameter?
  • Could a truthiness conversion accept "yes"?
  • Did the service mutate stored tasks?
  • Does the diff match the accepted plan?

If Agent mode fails during the demo, pairs can write the plan, a query-parsing truth table, four test names, and a change list by hand. Reveal the code afterward.

If something goes wrong:

  • Plan too broad: "Stop. Use only the three named files and show a revised plan."
  • Dependency proposed: reject it and restate the no-dependency constraint.
  • Test fails: ask for an explanation tied to one failing assertion before allowing a revision.
  • Repeated revisions with no progress: stop and describe the smallest acceptable correction.

"Agent mode fit because the change crossed related files and tests could guide each step. Other tasks need a different workflow."

docs.title: Segment 5: Chat, agent, or manual (0:43 to 0:50)
docs.text:
Use Chat to explain a problem, suggest options, or propose one small edit. Use an agent for clear multi-file outcomes with named tools and tests. Work manually when the change is tiny, requirements are unclear, or autonomy adds review work. Pause when permissions, data handling, or a destructive action is unresolved.

Task Start with Reason Explain a failing assertion Chat or inspection No multi-file action Rename a local variable Manual or inline The edit is small Add a route plus service tests Agent The files and tests are closely related Decide an authorization policy A person It's a policy decision

"You can redirect the agent or stop it. You don't have to follow its first plan."

docs.title: Exercise: redirect and stop (0:50 to 0:57)
docs.text:
Tell learners a proposal has started changing the response schema and package.json. The redirect:

Stop. Do not change package.json or the response schema.
Revert those proposed changes.
Keep the existing service API and add only the optional filter.
Show the revised plan before editing.

The revised plan returns to route, service, and tests, and the dependency and schema changes leave the proposed diff.

Then say an unexpected command requests network access. Learners choose stop and note the unresolved permission. Check that the revised file list matches the contract and nothing unrelated is still queued.

docs.title: Common questions
docs.text:
Should I approve every tool call so the agent can finish? No. Check why the action is needed, what it affects, and whether you can undo it. Reject or stop when the contract doesn't require it.

Is agent mode always better for multi-file work? No. Requirements, tests, risk, and review cost matter. Chat or manual work can give you more control.

What if it keeps fixing its own failures? Iteration helps only when each cycle improves the result. Stop repeated, broad, or unexplained changes and inspect the problem.

How do we know which files it read? Use the product's file list and repository tools. If you can't tell, stop.

What about MCP or external tools? Check the server, its permissions, and where data goes. The demo needs none.

docs.title: Pitfalls
docs.text: Pitfall Recovery "Fix the project" with no criteria Write one user-visible goal, non-goals, files, and tests Trusting the agent's test summary Run the focused test yourself Reviewing only the final message Read the full diff and command output A surprise dependency Reject it, restore the manifest, use existing APIs

docs.title: Close and lab handoff (0:57 to 1:00)
docs.text:
"Define the task before the agent starts. Use tests to check the result, then decide whether to accept it."

Open lab/README.md. Learners scaffold one Todo API, compare Ask and Agent mode on a feature, redirect a repository refactor, and decide whether to accept the work. Check that every learner has Agent mode before they start.
