docs.text: A reviewed handoff for POST /api/bookmarks containing the issue, implementation patch, test results, review decision, deviations, deferred scope, and next action.

docs.title: End-to-end capstone for one endpoint
docs.text: Session M6-02 | 3 hours

docs.title: One slice
docs.text:
Implement and review:

POST /api/bookmarks

Everything else is deferred.

docs.title: The result is a handoff
docs.text:
• implementation-ready issue;
  • implemented patch;
  • executable test results;
  • review decision;
  • deferred scope and next action.

docs.title: The scope lives in the issue
docs.text:
Implement only POST /api/bookmarks, use synthetic data, and keep the existing dependencies.

Stop if the work requires another endpoint, live data, deployment, tool configuration, or a new dependency.

docs.title: Session M5-02 is an input
docs.text:
The accepted specification must separate:

Behavior Implementation constraint Observable request and response rules Node.js, Express, in-memory storage Validation and duplicate behavior Existing dependencies only Acceptance scenarios Exact files and test command

docs.title: Issue trace
docs.text:
Every acceptance criterion maps to:

specification ID -> planned file -> executable test

If the issue adds behavior missing from the specification, revise the issue before implementation.

docs.title: Scope guard
docs.text:
In scope:

  • create one bookmark;
  • validate the accepted fields;
  • reject a duplicate URL;
  • return the documented envelope and status.

Out of scope: authentication, persistence, other endpoints, deployment, and new packages.

docs.title: When work is blocked
docs.text:
Use GitHub Copilot for the implementation.

Record the blocker and a request-changes or pause decision in the handoff. Resume the work before claiming completion.

docs.title: Run the tests
docs.text:
npm test

The suite checks success, defaults, field validation, and duplicate URLs.

docs.title: Review and handover
docs.text:
Trace the change back to the specification. Review the diff, test output, dependency change, and scope decisions in the issue. Record any deviation in the handoff.

Record one decision: approve, request changes, or pause.

docs.title: Lab time plan
docs.text: Phase Time Accept the specification and scope 25 min Write the issue and establish the baseline 25 min Implement the accepted slice 35 min Test, review, and hand off 35 min

docs.title: Lab
docs.text: Overview Lab Trainer Guide

docs.title: Session M6-02 lab: End-to-end capstone for one endpoint
docs.text:
Duration: 2 hours

Difficulty: Advanced

Prerequisites: Sessions M1-01 to M1-03, M2-01 to M2-04, M3-01 to M3-05 and M5-02; Session M5-01 is optional

docs.title: Before you start
docs.text:
You need repository or sandbox access, GitHub Copilot, Node.js 20 or later, a human reviewer, and synthetic bookmark data. Don't add a package, configure an MCP server, or use production data. The only slice is POST /api/bookmarks.

Phase Work Time 1 Set the boundary and accept the specification 25 min 2 Write the issue and establish the baseline 25 min 3 Implement the accepted slice 35 min 4 Test, review, and hand off 35 min

docs.title: Phase 1: Accept the specification and scope (25 min)
docs.text:
Read starter/bookmark-create-spec.md. Check it against the Session M5-02 standard:

  • requirements describe observable behavior;
  • acceptance scenarios are testable;
  • implementation choices appear only under constraints;
  • non-goals are named;
  • every open question has an owner or a safe default.

Record the accepted specification IDs and all scope decisions in the GitHub issue section of starter/capstone-handoff.md. Do not add requirements during implementation.

docs.title: Phase 2: Write the issue and establish the baseline (25 min)
docs.text:
Write the issue in starter/capstone-handoff.md. Include:

  • goal and accepted specification IDs;
  • acceptance criteria and non-goals;
  • expected files;
  • required tests;
  • work stop conditions;
  • human reviewer.

Copy and enter the starter project:

mkdir -p ~/copilot-labs/session-m6-02
cp -R lab/starter/capstone-project ~/copilot-labs/session-m6-02/capstone-project
cd ~/copilot-labs/session-m6-02/capstone-project
npm install

Run the health-check baseline:

npm test -- --runTestsByPath tests/health.test.js

Then run npm test. The Bookmark tests should fail because the route does not exist. Record that baseline. The missing-route failures are expected at this stage.

docs.title: Phase 3: Implement the accepted slice (35 min)
docs.text:
Use Copilot and treat the issue as the work order. Before editing, list the expected files and map each file to a specification ID.

Implement only:

  • route registration;
  • in-memory creation and duplicate lookup;
  • accepted field validation;
  • documented success and error responses.

Stop if the work requires another endpoint, live data, deployment, tool configuration, or a new dependency. If you are blocked or out of time, record the blocker in starter/capstone-handoff.md. Don't claim completion without test results.

docs.title: Phase 4: Test, review, and hand off (35 min)
docs.text:
Run:

npm test

Compare the patch with the issue and specification. Check that package.json contains no new dependency. Record any deviation from the accepted issue in the handoff.

Ask your reviewer to record one decision: approve, request changes, or pause. Complete every section in starter/capstone-handoff.md.

docs.title: Checkpoints
docs.text: Time Expected state 25 min Specification and scope review are complete 50 min Issue and executable baseline are recorded 85 min Patch is ready 105 min Tests and specification trace are reviewed 120 min Decision and next action are recorded

docs.title: Final deliverable
docs.text:
Submit one capstone-handoff.md containing:

  1. The implementation-ready issue mapped to specification IDs.
  2. The patch summary.
  3. Executable test results.
  4. The human review decision and reviewer.
  5. Deferred scope, deviations, and known risks.
  6. One next action with an owner.

docs.title: Trainer Guide
docs.text: Overview Lab Trainer Guide

docs.title: Session M6-02 trainer guide: End-to-end capstone for one endpoint
docs.text: 00:00 Start timer Reset timer Print guide      Enable timer shortcut (T)

docs.title: Goal
docs.text: Guide learners through one reviewed POST /api/bookmarks change with GitHub Copilot. Scope decisions live in the accepted GitHub issue, and the Session M5-02 specification standards apply. Don't let the exercise grow into a full API, deployment, or tool tour.

docs.title: One-hour plan
docs.text: Time Segment 0:00 to 0:08 Define the one-slice capstone 0:08 to 0:18 Set the issue boundary 0:18 to 0:30 Inspect and tighten the specification 0:30 to 0:40 Write the implementation issue 0:40 to 0:50 Walk through the patch and tests 0:50 to 1:00 Make the review decision and hand off

docs.title: Teach the boundary
docs.text:
The required slice is POST /api/bookmarks. Learners use GitHub Copilot to implement it, run the tests, and review the result with a person. Unfinished work isn't capstone completion.

Write these non-goals where everyone can see them:

  • no authentication;
  • no persistent storage;
  • no list, read, update, or delete endpoint;
  • no deployment or CI redesign;
  • no new dependency.

Learners put every scope decision in the accepted GitHub issue. They stop if the work needs another endpoint, live data, deployment, tool configuration, or a new dependency.

docs.title: Apply Session M5-02
docs.text:
Use lab/starter/bookmark-create-spec.md as the source for accepted behavior. Learners check that each requirement is observable, technology choices stay in the constraints section, and non-goals are named. They map each issue criterion to a specification ID and a test.

The issue names the exact route, response shapes, validation rules, duplicate behavior, expected files, required tests, reviewer, and stop conditions. It adds no behavior missing from the specification.

docs.title: Implementation walkthrough
docs.text:
Use this work order:

Implement only the accepted POST /api/bookmarks issue in the training sandbox.
Use synthetic data and the existing dependencies. Before editing, name the expected
files and map each change to a requirement. Run npm test. Stop if the work requires
another endpoint, live data, deployment, tool configuration, or a new dependency.
Report changed files, test results, deviations, and deferred scope for review.

After 30 minutes, check whether learners can finish in the segment. If blocked, they record the blocker and a request-changes or pause decision in the handoff.

docs.title: Review gate
docs.text:
1. Specification and acceptance criteria.
  2. Scope and deferrals.
  3. Validation, response shape, duplicate handling, and tests.
  4. Deviations from the accepted issue.
  5. Next action and its owner.

Record one decision: approve, request changes, or pause. Don't approve a change with a serious issue because time ran out.

docs.title: Reference assets
docs.text:
• lab/solution/capstone-project/: the creation endpoint and tests.
  • lab/solution/reference-handoff.md: the full issue-to-handoff record.
  • lab/starter/capstone-handoff.md: the learner template.
  • lab/starter/trainer-delivery-plan-template.md: optional trainer reflection, not a learner deliverable.

docs.title: Common questions
docs.text:
Should learners add the other Bookmark endpoints? No. Record them under deferred scope.

What if agent access fails? A patch plan isn't capstone completion.

What if the tests can't run? Record the command, the failure, findings from inspection, and the next action. Don't approve without executable test results.

docs.title: Session M7-01: Work effectively in the GitHub Copilot app
docs.text:
Open slides Slides in new tab Download PDF Close slides

Module: Product and Delivery Teams

Difficulty: Beginner

Prerequisites: A GitHub account with GitHub Copilot access

Duration: 3 hours (1 hour trainer content + 2 hours lab)

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
Start the Delivery Decision Studio path by comparing answers with and without repository context. Save what you learn in an initiative context brief. You check context usage, request an independent critique, and test whether a fresh session can use the brief without the original chat.

The fictional Service Request Portal is the shared scenario. You can use sanitized work from your own team instead.

Important

The GitHub Copilot app is required. Fix access and client problems before the lab.

docs.title: Learning outcomes
docs.text:
Learners can:

  1. Find and use Chats, Projects, My work, Search, Automations, and Customize.
  2. Choose Interactive, Plan, or Autopilot mode for a task with a defined scope.
  3. Add files with @, reference issues with #, and open commands with /.
  4. Choose repository, issue, file, or uploaded-document context for a question.
  5. Inspect the skills, agents, MCP servers, plugins, and canvases available to them.
  6. Explain the difference between an MCP connection and a plugin package.
  7. Check context usage and decide whether to compact or start fresh.
  8. Review and revise a proposed Markdown change.
  9. Update a context brief when new source information arrives.
  10. Request an independent critique before sharing the brief.

docs.title: Session structure
docs.text: Block Duration Material Trainer content 1 hour Trainer guide Lab 2 hours Lab guide

docs.title: Materials
docs.text: Resource Location Slides slides.md Starter initiative and brief template lab/starter/ Reference brief and context review lab/solution/

docs.title: Boundaries
docs.text:
• Use synthetic or sanitized material only.
  • Treat Copilot output as a proposal until you check its source.
  • No programming, Git command-line work, or extension development is required.
  • Delivery Decision Studio is the learning path. Service Request Portal is the initiative.

docs.title: Work effectively in the GitHub Copilot app
docs.text: Session M7-01 | Product and Delivery Teams | Beginner

docs.title: Work in the GitHub Copilot app
docs.text:
Work in the GitHub Copilot app with repository context. Save work that others can review.

Delivery Decision Studio is the six-session path. Service Request Portal is the initiative.

docs.title: Save work beyond the chat
docs.text:
Use the chat to work through an idea. Keep project context, source references, issues, and saved work available for review after the conversation ends.

Gather evidence → form a proposal → review it → save the decision → verify it

Check Copilot's explanation against the source facts.

docs.title: Context has a cost
docs.text:
Context choice When it helps One named file The answer depends on a specific rule or API A project or repository The task needs relationships across files An issue or pull request The task needs delivery history and discussion No repository context The work is general and contains no project facts

Tell Copilot why each source matters. Don't make it guess.

docs.title: Separate facts, assumptions, and decisions
docs.text:
Type Example Fact "Issue 42 names a response-time problem." Assumption "The mobile client uses the documented endpoint." Decision "The product owner will confirm the client behavior."

Separating these categories makes uncertainty visible.

docs.title: Know the main work areas
docs.text: Area Use it for Chats Exploration and interviews Projects Repository-grounded work My work Issues, pull requests, and sessions Search Finding repository information Automations Recurring or on-demand tasks Customize Skills, agents, MCP servers, and canvases

docs.title: Context comes before the prompt
docs.text:
Attach the smallest set of sources that answers the question.

Name the files, issues, or repository that should support the answer.

docs.title: Choose the session mode
docs.text:
Mode Use in this path Interactive Questions, interviews, and reviewed drafts Plan Review a multi-step approach before changes Autopilot Work with agreed scope and permission to act without review of every action

Session M7-01 uses Interactive, then Plan. The learner reviews every write.

docs.title: Use context controls
docs.text:
• @ adds a file.
  • # references an issue.
  • / opens commands.
  • /context shows current context usage.
  • /compact summarizes a long active session.
  • /clear or /reset starts fresh.

docs.title: Ask for sources
docs.text:
Explain the initiative for a product owner.
Cite the supplied source for each factual claim.
Mark missing information as unknown.

A confident answer without a source is still unverified.

docs.title: Inspect what Copilot can use
docs.text:
• Skills provide repeatable procedures.
  • Agents carry role-specific instructions and tools.
  • MCP servers connect Copilot to systems.
  • Plugins install reusable packages that can include MCP servers and other customizations.
  • Canvases provide visible shared state.
  • Automations repeat tasks with a defined scope.

Availability depends on the plan, policy, and installation.

docs.title: Use one repeatable work pattern
docs.text:
Read -> propose -> review -> write -> verify

Every later Module 7 session uses this pattern.

docs.title: Save the working brief
docs.text:
The lab creates initiative-context-brief.md with:

  • facts and sources;
  • unknowns;
  • useful GitHub artifacts;
  • the next decision and owner.

The brief must make sense without the chat history.

docs.title: Revise the brief when sources change
docs.text:
Initial source
  → first brief
  → approved late evidence
  → focused revision
  → fresh-session verification

Keep the brief consistent with the new source information.

docs.title: Lab
docs.text:
1. Open the repository as a Copilot project.
  2. Inspect the available capabilities.
  3. Start fresh without the source, then compare an unscoped answer with a grounded answer.
  4. Create and commit the initiative context brief.
  5. Apply approved late evidence.
  6. Review and commit the focused revision.
  7. Ask /rubber-duck for independent critique.
  8. Check the brief in a fresh session.

docs.title: Lab
docs.text: Overview Lab Trainer Guide

docs.title: Session M7-01 lab: Build and check a grounded working brief
docs.text:
Duration: 2 hours

Difficulty: Beginner

docs.title: What you will learn
docs.text:
Compare Copilot's answers with and without project context. Use the sourced information to write a brief, then revise it when new information arrives. Finally, check whether a fresh session can use the brief on its own.

Part Work Time 1 Check the app, mode, and project 15 min 2 Compare weak and grounded context 25 min 3 Create the first working brief 30 min 4 Update the brief with new source information 25 min 5 Check the brief in a fresh session 25 min

docs.title: Before you start
docs.text:
Complete the track capability setup.

You need GitHub Copilot app access, read access to the training repository project, and permission to create a branch or working copy for the brief.

docs.title: Part 1: Check the app and project (15 minutes)
docs.text:
1. Open the training repository under Projects.
  2. Start an interactive session.
  3. Select Interactive mode. Type @ and add lab/starter/initiative-overview.md.
  4. Ask Copilot to report the file name and its first heading.
  5. Open Customize → Installed and inspect the visible skills, MCP servers, plugins, and canvases.
  6. Run /context.

Use Interactive for the comparison. Switch to Plan before asking Copilot to propose repository changes. Don't use Autopilot here, because you review each write.

@ adds files, # references issues, and / opens commands. Type the character and select the item from the picker. A typed file token alone doesn't attach the source.

Checkpoint: Copilot can read the supplied file, and you can identify which capabilities are available.

docs.title: Part 2: Compare weak and grounded context (25 minutes)
docs.text:
Start a fresh session with /clear or /reset so the file read in Part 1 isn't carried over. Don't attach the initiative file yet. Start with this deliberately weak prompt:

Explain the Service Request Portal initiative, its users, constraints, and next
decision. Mark anything uncertain.

Identify statements that have no visible source.

Now attach starter/initiative-overview.md and ask:

Use only @initiative-overview.md. Explain the requested outcome, affected users,
known constraints, and next decision. Cite the heading that supports each fact.
Keep missing information as unknown.

Compare the answers:

Check Unscoped answer Grounded answer Unsupported facts Visible unknowns Source references Useful next decision

Checkpoint: Explain which answer is safer and how repository context changed it.

docs.title: Part 3: Create the first working brief (30 minutes)
docs.text:
Copy the templates:

cp sessions/session-m7-01-copilot-app-foundations/lab/starter/initiative-context-brief-template.md \
  docs/discovery/initiative-context-brief.md

Ask Copilot to complete the brief from initiative-overview.md. Require:

  • the requested outcome and affected users;
  • known facts with section references;
  • assumptions separated from unknowns;
  • named non-goals;
  • the next decision and its owner;
  • the relevant capabilities found in Part 1.

Review the proposed change before accepting it. Reject any statement that has no source, invents an owner, or turns an unknown into a fact.

Commit the first version:

git add docs/discovery/initiative-context-brief.md
git commit -m "Create grounded initiative working brief"

Checkpoint: Your brief separates source facts, assumptions, unknowns, and the next decision clearly enough for someone to use it without reading the chat.

docs.title: Part 4: Update the brief with new source information (25 minutes)
docs.text:
Open starter/late-evidence.md. Treat it as source information that arrived after the first brief was committed.

Ask Copilot to:

  1. compare the new information with the saved brief;
  2. list which sections need to change;
  3. identify any resolved unknown;
  4. identify any statement that is now contradicted;
  5. propose a focused file update.

Review the diff. Do not rewrite unrelated sections.

Commit the revision:

git add docs/discovery/initiative-context-brief.md
git commit -m "Update working brief with approved evidence"

Checkpoint: Git history shows which source changes led to the revision.

docs.title: Part 5: Check the brief in a fresh session (25 minutes)
docs.text:
Before starting fresh, run /context. If the current session is crowded but the thread still matters, use /compact. For the fresh-session check, use /clear or /reset, then attach only docs/discovery/initiative-context-brief.md.

Ask:

Using only this working brief, report:
1. the requested outcome;
2. supported facts and their sources;
3. unresolved decisions;
4. named non-goals;
5. the next owner action.
Do not infer missing information.

Compare the answer with the file. If it misses or misstates any item, correct the brief so the new session has what it needs.

Run an independent critique:

/rubber-duck Review the initiative context brief for unsupported claims,
ambiguous ownership, hidden customer references, and decisions presented as facts.

docs.title: Final deliverable
docs.text:
Submit:

  1. docs/discovery/initiative-context-brief.md;
  2. two commits showing the first brief and the revision based on the new source.

Session M7-02 uses this brief as the source for its decision interview.

docs.text: Overview Lab Trainer Guide

docs.title: Session M7-01 trainer guide: Work effectively in the GitHub Copilot app
docs.text:
00:00 Start timer Reset timer Print guide Enable timer shortcut (T)

Duration: 1 hour Audience: Product managers, product owners, business analysts, project managers, and delivery leads

docs.title: Goal
docs.text: Show learners how to choose a session mode and attach source material in the GitHub Copilot app. Compare answers with and without those sources before creating the first Delivery Decision Studio brief.

docs.title: One-hour plan
docs.text: Time Segment 0:00-0:08 Orient learners to the app 0:08-0:18 Choose mode and context 0:18-0:28 Inspect capabilities and context usage 0:28-0:40 Compare unscoped and grounded answers 0:40-0:53 Create, revise, and check a working brief 0:53-1:00 Launch the lab

docs.title: Prepare
docs.text:
• Every learner can open the GitHub Copilot app, start a chat, and open the training repository as a project.
  • Open the starter initiative and reference brief.
  • Use only the fictional scenario in the demo.

A generic chatbot doesn't meet this session's goal. Use the app and the repository.

docs.title: Teach the app as a work environment
docs.text:
• Chats: exploratory work and interviews;
  • Projects: repository-grounded work;
  • My work: issues, pull requests, and active agent sessions;
  • Search: finding repository information;
  • Automations: recurring or on-demand tasks;
  • Customize: skills, agents, MCP servers, plugins, and canvases.

Labels move. Teach what each area is for, not a fixed click path.

docs.title: Modes and context syntax
docs.text:
• Interactive: interviews, source checks, and reviewed drafts.
  • Plan: before a multi-step change, so the learner approves the plan.
  • Autopilot: work with agreed scope where you don't review every action. Not used for the M7-01 write.

@ adds files, # references issues, and / opens commands. Run /context before the first draft. Use /compact only to keep a long thread. Use /clear or /reset for the fresh-session test.

docs.title: Context before prompting
docs.text:
Attach the smallest set of sources that answers the question.

Contrast:

Explain this project.

with:

Use the repository overview and the open initiative notes. Explain the product,
the affected users, the current decision, and the missing information for a
product owner. Cite the source for each factual claim.

Ask learners which sources Copilot used and which statements remain uncertain.

docs.title: Capability inspection
docs.text:
Open Customize and identify what is available. Explain:

  • a skill provides a repeatable procedure;
  • an agent carries role-specific instructions and tools;
  • an MCP server lets Copilot read or act in another system;
  • a plugin is an installable package that can bundle skills, agents, hooks, MCP servers, or canvases;
  • a canvas provides visible shared state;
  • an automation repeats a task with a defined scope.

Learners don't build these here. Availability depends on plan, policy, and installation.

docs.title: Demo: create and revise a saved brief
docs.text:
1. Start a fresh session and ask for an initiative summary without the source.
  2. Mark unsupported statements.
  3. Attach lab/starter/initiative-overview.md and ask again with source references.
  4. Ask Copilot to complete initiative-context-brief-template.md.
  5. Review and commit the brief.
  6. Reveal lab/starter/late-evidence.md.
  7. Ask Copilot for a focused update and review the diff.
  8. Run /rubber-duck for an independent critique.
  9. Start a fresh session with only the saved brief. Check it can identify the outcome, facts, unresolved decisions, non-goals, and next owner action.

The pattern for every later session:

Read -> propose -> review -> write -> verify

docs.title: Session M7-02: Interview ideas and shape better work
docs.text:
Open slides Slides in new tab Download PDF Close slides

Module: Product and Delivery Teams

Difficulty: Beginner

Prerequisites: Session M7-01 and working GitHub Copilot access

Duration: 3 hours (1 hour trainer content + 2 hours lab)

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
Continue the Delivery Decision Studio path with your Session M7-01 context brief. Install the supplied project skill and use it to ask questions in dependency order. Turn the approved answers into a decision brief and issue proposal. When a late constraint arrives, revise only the affected decisions.

The fictional Service Request Portal remains the initiative.

Important

GitHub Copilot is required.

docs.title: Learning outcomes
docs.text:
Learners can:

  • Install and check the supplied decision-interview project skill.
  • Run a GitHub Copilot interview that asks only questions whose prerequisites are settled.
  • Resolve scope, constraints, success, failure, ownership, and approval.
  • Review Copilot recommendations before accepting or revising them.
  • Create a reviewed Markdown decision brief in the repository.
  • Draft an issue proposal with testable acceptance criteria and a definition of done.
  • Reopen only the decisions affected by new source information.
  • Check that the revised brief and issue proposal agree.
  • Check context usage before each interview round and start fresh for the final review.
  • Request an independent critique before approving the brief and proposal.
  • Assign an owner and reviewer before work enters a sprint.

docs.title: Session flow
docs.text:
Vague request
  -> project skill installation
  -> GitHub Copilot decision interview
  -> human review and decisions
  -> Markdown decision brief
  -> GitHub issue proposal
  -> acceptance criteria
  -> definition of done

docs.title: Session structure
docs.text: Block Duration Material Trainer content 1 hour Trainer guide Lab 2 hours Lab guide

docs.title: Materials
docs.text: Resource Location Marp slides slides.md Starter request and repository templates lab/starter/ Completed Copilot-reviewed examples lab/solution/

docs.title: Boundaries
docs.text:
• Teach the interview pattern, not skill authoring. Learners install and use the supplied skill without editing it.
  • Use sanitized material only. Treat Copilot questions, recommendations, and drafts as proposals.
  • Product and approval decisions stay with named people.
  • Don't create or update a live work item until the request owner approves the brief. Session M7-03 creates the approved GitHub issues.

docs.title: Interview ideas and shape better work
docs.text: Session M7-02 | Product and Delivery Teams | 3 hours

docs.title: GitHub Copilot is required
docs.text:
Before the session:

  • Copy the supplied project skill to .github/skills/decision-interview/SKILL.md.
  • Start a new project session.
  • Check decision-interview under Customize → Skills.
  • Run /decision-interview with the short test request.

docs.title: Start with the actual problem
docs.text:
"Make request status clearer so people stop asking support."

Before this idea can enter a sprint, decide who it serves and what it changes. You also need decisions about data, scope, ownership, and approval.

The Delivery Decision Studio path carries the Session M7-01 context brief into this interview. Service Request Portal remains the initiative.

docs.title: The shaping flow
docs.text:
Vague request
  -> project skill installation
  -> GitHub Copilot decision interview
  -> human decisions
  -> Markdown decision brief
  -> GitHub issue proposal
  -> acceptance criteria
  -> definition of done

Don't jump from one sentence to an issue template.

The project skill keeps this method consistent. It doesn't make the decisions.

docs.title: Interview as a decision tree
docs.text:
Each answer can raise new questions.

Ask the current frontier: every decision the owner can make now without guessing about an unsettled decision.

Questions that depend on this round wait for the next round.

docs.title: Work in rounds
docs.text:
Round 1: outcome, affected user, current pain
Round 2: scope, current state, constraints
Round 3: success, failure, edge cases
Round 4: owner, reviewer, approval, rollout

Ask GitHub Copilot to work out the next frontier from the answers the owner accepted.

Use Interactive mode for each frontier. Switch to Plan before proposed file changes. Autopilot is outside this interview.

docs.title: Check context between rounds
docs.text:
• Run /context.
  • Use /compact only when the same thread must continue.
  • Use /clear or /reset when old assumptions are polluting the interview.
  • Resume with the approved context and the owner's settled decisions, not a transcript.

docs.title: Give a recommendation
docs.text:
For each question:

  1. State the decision clearly.
  2. Offer concrete choices when useful.
  3. Recommend an answer and explain the tradeoff.
  4. Wait for the request owner to decide.

GitHub Copilot frames the choice. A person owns the choice.

docs.title: Facts and decisions are different
docs.text:
Use approved sources for facts Ask people for decisions Existing workflow Which users are in scope Current labels or fields Which behavior should change Known technical limits Which tradeoff to accept Policy and data rules Who approves release

Mark unsupported claims as unverified.

docs.title: Settle six decision areas
docs.text:
• Scope: who and what are included?
  • Constraints: what limits the solution?
  • Success: what result will show that the change helped?
  • Failure: what can go wrong, and what should happen?
  • Ownership: who decides and who maintains it?
  • Approval: who reviews the brief and accepts the work?

Keep unresolved decisions visible.

docs.title: The decision brief
docs.text:
A useful brief records:

  • problem and target outcome;
  • users, scope, and exclusions;
  • constraints and dependencies;
  • success and failure measures;
  • settled decisions and open questions;
  • owner, reviewer, and who approves the brief and when.

Keep it short enough to review in one sitting.

docs.title: Create a GitHub issue proposal
docs.text:
Ask GitHub Copilot to draft:

  • user and outcome;
  • defined scope and non-goals;
  • acceptance criteria;
  • dependencies and risks;
  • owner and reviewer;
  • definition of done.

Compare the draft with the approved brief. Each field should trace to an approved answer or an open question.

Session M7-03 creates the approved issues through GitHub MCP.

docs.title: Reopen only the affected branch
docs.text:
New source information changes requester and support visibility.

Approved brief
  + new visibility constraint
  → reopen visibility decisions
  → update affected criteria
  → preserve unrelated decisions

Do not restart the interview or rewrite settled scope without new source information.

docs.title: Check in a fresh session
docs.text:
Give a new session only:

  • the revised decision brief;
  • the revised issue proposal.

Ask it to find contradictions, unresolved owners, and acceptance criteria with no source decision.

The fresh session shows which assumptions you left in the conversation instead of recording in the files.

Then use /rubber-duck to challenge unsupported criteria, hidden scope, and missing owners.

docs.title: Acceptance criteria describe testable behavior
docs.text:
Weak:

Status is easy to understand.

Testable:

A requester can see the current status and last updated time for each submitted request.

Include a failure case when the feature can mislead, expose data, or block progress.

docs.title: Define what the team needs before release
docs.text:
Acceptance criteria describe product behavior.

Definition of done covers the work needed to release and hand over safely:

  • criteria reviewed;
  • permissions checked;
  • supported states documented;
  • test or review results attached;
  • product and service owners approve.

docs.title: Azure Boards update paths
docs.text:
The interview always runs with GitHub Copilot.

Azure Boards path Method MCP Copilot prepares and reviews the approved update before the MCP tool sends it Browser Copilot prepares the exact values, then the learner enters and checks them

There is no static or no-Copilot route.

docs.title: Lab deliverables
docs.text:
1. The installed decision-interview project skill.
  2. A revised decision brief.
  3. An aligned GitHub issue proposal.
  4. Any fixes made after the fresh-session check.

The request owner decides whether the brief is ready for issue planning.

docs.title: Lab
docs.text: Overview Lab Trainer Guide

docs.title: Session M7-02 lab: Interview a request and revise the decision brief
docs.text:
Duration: 2 hours

Difficulty: Beginner

Prerequisites: Session M7-01 and working GitHub Copilot app access

docs.title: What you will learn
docs.text:
Install a repository skill and use it to interview the request owner. Turn the decisions into a brief and issue proposal. When a late constraint arrives, revise the affected decisions and check that both files still agree.

Part Work Time 1 Install and check the interview skill 20 min 2 Run the first decision interview 35 min 3 Create the decision brief and issue proposal 25 min 4 Reopen one branch for a late constraint 25 min 5 Check readiness in a fresh session 15 min

docs.title: Before you start
docs.text:
Complete the track capability setup.

Use the Session M7-01 initiative-context-brief.md. If the trainer is delivering Session M7-02 alone, use starter/vague-request.md.

docs.title: Part 1: Install and check the interview skill (20 minutes)
docs.text:
Copy the supplied project skill into the root of the training repository:

mkdir -p .github/skills/decision-interview
cp sessions/session-m7-02-interview-and-shape-work/lab/starter/.github/skills/decision-interview/SKILL.md \
  .github/skills/decision-interview/SKILL.md
git add .github/skills/decision-interview/SKILL.md
git commit -m "Add decision interview skill"

Open a new GitHub Copilot app session for the project. Open Customize → Skills → Installed and check that decision-interview appears.

Select Interactive mode for the interview. Use Plan only when Copilot proposes file changes. Don't use Autopilot: the request owner answers each round.

Run a short test:

/decision-interview

Test request: Add a clearer request status.
Ask only the first decision frontier, then stop.

If the skill does not appear:

  1. check the file is at .github/skills/decision-interview/SKILL.md;
  2. check the skill name and description are present in its frontmatter;
  3. reopen the project or start a new session.

Copilot CLI users can run /skills reload and /skills info decision-interview.

Checkpoint: Copilot invokes the supplied skill and returns a numbered first round of questions, not a drafted work item.

docs.title: Part 2: Run the first decision interview (35 minutes)
docs.text:
Attach the Session M7-01 working brief or starter/vague-request.md, then run:

/decision-interview

Interview me as the request owner. Use only the attached source. Continue until
scope, users, success, failure, ownership, approval, and non-goals are decided or
assigned as open questions.

For each frontier (the decisions whose prerequisites are settled):

  1. answer as the request owner;
  2. accept, reject, or revise each recommendation;
  3. require Copilot to restate the decision and reason;
  4. check that dependent questions wait for earlier decisions;
  5. ask for the next frontier.

Stop when each branch has a decision or a named open question.

After each round, run /context. Use /compact only if the interview must remain in the same session and context pressure is high. If the interview has drifted, use /clear or /reset, attach the approved context brief, and provide only the decisions the owner has settled and the open questions needed to continue.

Checkpoint: As the request owner, you can state the settled decisions, their reasons, and the open questions without relying on the chat transcript.

docs.title: Part 3: Create the decision brief and issue proposal (25 minutes)
docs.text:
Ask Copilot to create:

  • docs/discovery/decision-brief.md from starter/decision-brief-template.md;
  • docs/discovery/issue-proposal.md from starter/issue-proposal-template.md.

Review both changes before accepting them.

The brief must separate:

  • facts from the source;
  • request-owner decisions;
  • unresolved questions and owners;
  • in-scope and out-of-scope behavior;
  • results that show success or failure;
  • approval state.

The issue proposal must trace each acceptance criterion to the approved brief. Do not create the GitHub issue yet.

Commit the first accepted versions.

docs.title: Part 4: Reopen one branch for a late constraint (25 minutes)
docs.text:
Open starter/late-constraint.md.

Run the skill again:

/decision-interview

Use the approved decision brief and @late-constraint.md. Reopen only the branches
affected by the new constraint. Show which prior decisions remain unchanged.

Answer the new frontier as the request owner. Update the decision brief and issue proposal.

Review the diff:

  • unchanged decisions should remain stable;
  • changed decisions should include a reason;
  • acceptance criteria should reflect the new constraint;
  • the issue proposal should contain no decision absent from the brief.

Commit the revision separately.

Checkpoint: Your repository history shows which decisions changed without rewriting the rest of the brief and proposal.

docs.title: Part 5: Check readiness in a fresh session (15 minutes)
docs.text:
Start a new session with /clear or /reset. Attach only the decision brief and issue proposal.

Ask Copilot to report:

  1. the approved outcome and non-goals;
  2. each acceptance criterion and its source decision;
  3. unresolved questions and owners;
  4. any contradiction between the two files;
  5. a readiness result: Ready, Revise, or Blocked.

Fix any contradiction and rerun the check.

Then request independent critique:

/rubber-duck Challenge the decision brief and issue proposal. Find unsupported
criteria, hidden scope, missing owners, and conflicts with the late constraint.

docs.title: Final deliverable
docs.text:
Submit:

  1. the installed decision-interview project skill;
  2. the approved decision brief;
  3. the aligned issue proposal;
  4. any fixes made after the fresh-session check.

Session M7-03 uses the approved brief and issue proposal to create live GitHub issues.

docs.title: Trainer supplement: Shape a requirement in Azure Boards
docs.text:
Use GitHub Copilot to interview the request owner, review a seeded Azure Boards requirement, and prepare approved updates.

Time: Use the two-hour Session M7-02 lab plan. This companion replaces Phases 4 and 5.

Important

The trainer must select and prepare this route before the workshop. It is not part of the standard learner path.

docs.title: Deliverable
docs.text:
Record these items in work-item-update-plan.md:

  • the approved decisions;
  • planned field changes;
  • the saved field values;
  • open gaps and next action;
  • the IDs of child Tasks created after the parent update.

docs.title: Prepare
docs.text:
You need:

  • the supplied decision-interview project skill;
  • a request owner and delivery reviewer;
  • the seeded Show request status in the portal requirement in a training project;
  • an Azure Boards browser session or an MCP connection that can read and update work items.

Before starting:

  1. Run one prompt and one follow-up in GitHub Copilot.
  2. Open ../starter/vague-request.md and work-item-update-plan.md.
  3. Open the seeded requirement. Check the title and the session-m7-02 and service-request-portal tags.
  4. Record the current description, acceptance criteria, priority, state, board column, and readiness value.
  5. Check which field, board column, or tag represents readiness.
  6. Check the reset method.

If Azure Boards MCP is unavailable, use the browser. Don't configure a new organization, process, field, or MCP server during the lab.

docs.title: Boundaries
docs.text:
• Use only the fictional Service Request Portal item.
  • Read the item before proposing an update. Treat every Copilot change as a draft.
  • Don't change area paths, iteration paths, identities, links, process settings, or team settings.
  • Don't create child Tasks until the request owner records approval.
  • Change only the seeded requirement and Tasks created by your pair. Never delete the seeded requirement.

docs.title: Phase 1: Run the Copilot interview
docs.text:
Run the decision-tree interview against:

Make request status clearer so people stop asking support.

Work through the branches for scope, constraints, success, failure, ownership, and approval. Settle each branch or assign its open question to an owner. Record the approved decisions in the update plan.

Ask the request owner to check that the recorded decisions match what you agreed before you review Azure Boards.

docs.title: Phase 2: Compare the findings with the requirement
docs.text:
Read the seeded item without changing it. Ask GitHub Copilot to compare the current fields with the approved decisions.

Field Review question Description Does it name the user, current problem, target outcome, scope, and non-goals? Acceptance criteria Can a reviewer observe the main path, permission boundary, stale or unmapped state, and excluded behavior? Priority Does the value match approved impact and urgency? State Does the state match the request owner's decision? Board column Is the item still in refinement, or is it approved for planning? Readiness Does the team's existing field, column, or tag state readiness?

Record the current value, Copilot proposal, reason, and owner decision. A field may stay unchanged.

docs.title: Phase 3: Prepare the update
docs.text:
Ask GitHub Copilot to draft exact field values from the approved decisions.

For the supplied scenario, use these expected changes to review the draft:

Field Proposed direction Description Cover facilities and equipment requesters, the public status label and latest update date, and named exclusions. Acceptance criteria Add requester-only access, the two permitted requester fields, stale and unmapped application behavior, support-only detail, and unchanged behavior for excluded request types. Priority Propose 1 and record the 20% contact-reduction target as the reason. The request owner may choose another value. State Use the team's approved state for an item that can enter planning. Board column Move from New only after approval. Use the team's existing ready-for-planning column. Readiness Set the existing readiness field or tag to the team's ready value.

Do not save yet.

docs.title: Phase 4: Request owner approval
docs.text:
Show the request owner:

  1. the approved decisions;
  2. the field comparison;
  3. the exact proposed values;
  4. the proposed child Tasks.

The request owner records:

  • Approved: update the parent, then create the approved child Tasks.
  • Approved with changes: revise the proposal, record the changes, then update.
  • Needs another interview round: return to the open branches. Do not update the item.

Silence isn't approval. The delivery reviewer can't approve for the request owner.

docs.title: MCP path
docs.text:
Use the approved Azure Boards MCP connection to:

  1. read the seeded requirement;
  2. prepare an update request without sending it;
  3. compare the request with the update plan;
  4. update only accepted fields;
  5. read the item again and record the saved values;
  6. create child Tasks after the parent matches the approval;
  7. read the parent links and record the Task IDs.

If MCP cannot show the pending update or read back the saved result, use the browser path.

docs.title: Browser path
docs.text:
1. Use the Copilot draft as the source for each accepted value.
  2. Edit only the accepted description, acceptance criteria, priority, state, board column, and readiness field or tag.
  3. Compare the form with the update plan.
  4. Save the requirement.
  5. Reopen it and record the saved values.
  6. Create only the approved child Tasks.
  7. Check each Task links to the seeded requirement.

Do not use bulk edit.

docs.title: Child Task gate
docs.text:
Create child Tasks only after the request owner accepts the parent changes. The supplied scenario normally needs two:

  • implement the requester status view and safe application fallback behavior;
  • validate state mapping, freshness behavior, and requester-only access.

Give each Task a clear result and owner role. If a blocking decision remains open, leave the child Task table empty.

docs.title: Review and deliver
docs.text: Check that saved fields match the update plan, acceptance criteria include positive and failure behavior, readiness didn't move while a blocking decision was open, and every created Task links to the parent. Fix mismatches and list unresolved gaps with an owner and next action.

docs.title: Reset and cleanup
docs.text:
Use the trainer's reset method. If the trainer directs cleanup in the browser or through MCP:

  1. Remove only child Tasks created by your pair.
  2. Restore only the fields listed in the trainer's seed record.
  3. Read the item again.
  4. Check the seeded title, tags, field values, and empty child-link list.

If you cannot prove that your pair created a child Task, leave it in place and tell the trainer.

docs.title: Trainer Guide
docs.text: Overview Lab Trainer Guide

docs.title: Session M7-02 trainer guide: Interview ideas and shape better work
docs.text: 00:00 Start timer Reset timer Print guide      Enable timer shortcut (T)

docs.title: Goal
docs.text: Show how the supplied decision-interview project skill uses the Session M7-01 context brief to turn an unclear request into a reviewed decision brief and issue proposal.

docs.title: One-hour plan
docs.text: Time Segment 0:00-0:06 Show the vague request and the cost of guessing 0:06-0:15 Explain the decision tree, frontier, and rounds 0:15-0:25 Model strong Copilot questions and recommendations 0:25-0:42 Run the Service Request Portal interview with GitHub Copilot 0:42-0:51 Review the answers and build a decision brief 0:51-0:57 Convert the brief into a GitHub issue proposal 0:57-1:00 Explain the lab and review roles

docs.title: Prepare
docs.text:
• Every learner can open the GitHub Copilot app and the training repository project.
  • Copy the supplied skill to .github/skills/decision-interview/SKILL.md.
  • In a new app session, check decision-interview appears under Customize → Skills → Installed.
  • Run /decision-interview with the short test request from the lab, plus one follow-up answer.
  • Interactive, Plan, and Autopilot modes are visible. The interview uses Interactive; file changes use Plan.
  • /context, /compact, /clear or /reset, and /rubber-duck appear in the command picker.
  • Open the starter templates and completed solution in separate windows.
  • Assign a request owner and delivery reviewer for each pair.

For a trainer-only Azure Boards delivery, learners need an MCP connection or the browser. Azure Boards changes only the update method. GitHub Copilot still runs the interview.

docs.title: The frontier controls question order
docs.text:
The frontier is the set of decisions the owner can make now because their prerequisites are settled. Ask all of them in one round. Hold any question that depends on a decision still open.

Don't ask for notification wording before the group decides whether the first release includes notifications. Don't ask for a success target before the group agrees on the problem and affected user.

docs.title: Recommendations make choices easier to review
docs.text:
Each Copilot question includes a recommended answer with its reasoning. The owner accepts or revises it.

Q1: Target user
Which group has the problem in the first release?

Recommendation: Start with employees who submitted a request. Leave service agents
out of the first release because they already have an internal queue.

docs.title: Facts don't belong in the decision queue
docs.text:
Copilot reads facts such as current status values, portal fields, or published retention rules from the sources. The request owner decides product behavior, tradeoffs, ownership, and approval.

When a source is unavailable, mark the claim as unverified. Don't turn it into a question for the owner.

docs.title: Check context between rounds
docs.text: Run /context after each round. Compact only when the same thread must continue. Start fresh when old recommendations leak into new decisions, carrying only the settled decisions and open questions. The decision brief becomes the record.

docs.title: Use an independent critic
docs.text: Before approval, run /rubber-duck against the brief and issue proposal. It looks for unsupported criteria, missing owners, hidden scope, and visibility-rule conflicts. The request owner decides which feedback to apply.

docs.title: Demonstration scenario
docs.text:
Start with:

Make request status clearer so people stop asking support.

Run it through /decision-interview. The skill asks a numbered frontier and waits for owner decisions instead of drafting the final brief.

docs.title: Round 1: Define the problem
docs.text:
1. Who is asking for updates?
  2. What do they need to know?
  3. What business or service problem should change?

Recommended direction: people who submitted a request need a plain-language status and recent update. Aim first to reduce manual "what is happening?" contacts. Leave service-process redesign out.

docs.title: Round 2: Set the scope
docs.text:
1. Which request types are included?
  2. Which existing states can the portal expose?
  3. Are email, chat, or mobile notifications included?
  4. What data must remain hidden?

Recommended direction: facilities and equipment requests in the web portal. Show a mapped public status, last updated time, and safe summary. Exclude outbound notifications, internal notes, agent names, and security details.

docs.title: Round 3: Define success and failure
docs.text:
1. How will the team know the change helped?
  2. What must never happen?
  3. What should the requester see when a status is missing or stale?
  4. Which accessibility and permission checks apply?

Recommended direction: fewer status-chasing contacts, and every supported request shows a public status. Failure includes exposing internal notes, showing a status to the wrong requester, or presenting stale data as current.

docs.title: Round 4: Close ownership and approval
docs.text:
1. Who owns the public status mapping?
  2. Who approves the decision brief?
  3. Who validates service behavior and access rules?
  4. Who can approve release?

Recommended direction: the portal product owner owns the work item. The service operations manager approves wording and state mapping. The privacy reviewer checks data exposure. The product owner accepts the completed work after test or review results are attached.

docs.title: Build the decision brief
docs.text:
Ask Copilot to create docs/discovery/decision-brief.md from the accepted answers. Review:

  • problem and target outcome;
  • users and scope;
  • non-goals;
  • constraints and dependencies;
  • success and failure measures;
  • decisions and open questions;
  • owner, reviewers, and approver.

Keep it short enough to review in one sitting.

docs.title: Build the issue proposal
docs.text:
Ask Copilot to convert the approved brief into an issue proposal:

  1. Write one user outcome.
  2. Copy the agreed scope and non-goals.
  3. Turn success and failure cases into testable acceptance criteria.
  4. Add dependencies and open risks.
  5. Name the owner and reviewer.
  6. Add a definition of done that covers test or review results and approval.

Learners check every drafted field against the approved brief. Session M7-03 creates the approved issues through GitHub MCP.

docs.title: Reopen an affected branch
docs.text: Reveal lab/starter/late-constraint.md. Ask the skill to reopen only visibility decisions. Requesters may now see only the public status label and latest update date, so the earlier requester summary goes. Authorized support staff may see the detailed status reason. Request types, notification exclusion, and ownership stay unchanged while the affected criteria are revised.

docs.title: Facilitation notes
docs.text:
• Ask no more than four questions in a demonstration round.
  • Let the request owner reject recommendations. A visible correction shows who owns the decision.
  • Keep unresolved items in an open-questions table with an owner and due point.
  • Push back on "easy," "fast," or "clear" without a result someone can check.
  • Skip estimation. The goal is readiness.

docs.title: Lab launch
docs.text: Learners use the Service Request Portal context from Session M7-01 or ../lab/starter/vague-request.md. Each learner or pair needs a request owner and delivery reviewer. The owner approves the decision brief. The reviewer checks the brief and proposal in a fresh session.

docs.title: Trainer-only Azure Boards supplement
docs.text: Use ../lab/azure-boards/README.md when learners have a seeded training requirement. It replaces work-item drafting in Phases 4 and 5. Check the field labels for priority and readiness first. Learners may use MCP or the browser to apply approved changes. The standard learner path stays in GitHub.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: Overview Lab Trainer Guide

docs.title: Session M7-03: Plan work with GitHub Issues and MCP
docs.text:
Open slides Slides in new tab Download PDF Close slides

Module: Product and Delivery Teams

Difficulty: Intermediate

Prerequisites: Sessions M7-01 to M7-02, GitHub Copilot app access, and an approved GitHub MCP connection

Duration: 3 hours (1 hour trainer content + 2 hours lab)

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
Continue the Delivery Decision Studio path by turning the approved Session M7-02 decision brief into a GitHub issue hierarchy. Check the GitHub MCP connection and inspect the repository before you plan any writes. Preview the full issue set in Markdown, create the approved issues, then read them back from GitHub to check and correct the result. The created GitHub issues are authoritative.

Learners use MCP tools. They don't build an MCP server.

Important

You need the GitHub MCP connection and write access to the training repository.

docs.title: Learning outcomes
docs.text:
1. Explain what an MCP server lets Copilot do.
  2. Inspect the GitHub tools available to the current session.
  3. Split an approved outcome into a parent issue and child issues with defined scope.
  4. Review issue titles, descriptions, acceptance criteria, dependencies, and ownership.
  5. Approve a GitHub write operation only after checking its target and arguments.
  6. Retrieve the created issues and compare them with the approved plan.
  7. Preview, apply, and check a focused correction.
  8. Classify concrete existing issues as duplicate, partial overlap, conflict, or unrelated.
  9. Leave a checked live issue set that Session M7-04 can read directly.

docs.title: Session structure
docs.text: Block Duration Material Trainer content 1 hour Trainer guide Lab 2 hours Lab guide

docs.title: Materials
docs.text: Resource Location Slides slides.md Approved brief and templates lab/starter/ Reference preview lab/solution/

docs.title: Boundaries
docs.text:
• Work only in the training repository.
  • Read before writing. Have Copilot show the complete issue set before creation.
  • The issue-plan Markdown is a temporary preview. After creation, the live issues are the record.
  • Check every created issue through a fresh GitHub read.
  • A plugin can package an MCP server, but check that the GitHub connection itself is active.

docs.title: Plan work with GitHub Issues and MCP
docs.text: Session M7-03 | Product and Delivery Teams | Intermediate

docs.title: Turn the brief into GitHub issues
docs.text:
Session M7-02 produced an approved decision brief.

Session M7-03 turns it into real GitHub issues.

This is the third step in Delivery Decision Studio.

docs.title: MCP in one sentence
docs.text:
An MCP server gives Copilot named tools for reading or changing another system.

You use the tools in this session without building the server.

docs.title: Write issues others can act on
docs.text:
The issue should let a contributor decide whether they can start, what success looks like, and who will review it.

Issue element What it prevents Outcome Work that repeats a vague request Results needed for acceptance "Done" without a way to prove it Non-goal Scope growth during implementation Dependency Work that starts before a needed decision Ownership gap Silent assumptions about who decides

Write enough detail for the next contributor to act.

docs.title: Parent and child issues answer different questions
docs.text:
The parent issue holds the outcome, shared constraints, and review path. Each child issue owns one independently reviewable result.

Parent: Improve request-status visibility
  ├─ Child: Public status mapping
  ├─ Child: Requester status view
  ├─ Child: Empty and stale states
  └─ Child: Requester-access verification

If two child issues must edit the same behavior at the same time, sequence them or clarify the design first.

docs.title: Review each MCP write
docs.text:
Copilot can prepare the issue plan. A person approves the write only after seeing the target repository and expected result.

After the write, fetch the issue again. Compare what GitHub stored with the approved plan instead of relying on the tool's success message.

The Markdown plan is a temporary preview. The created GitHub issues are authoritative.

docs.title: Read before writing
docs.text:
1. Check the repository.
  2. Inspect existing labels and milestones.
  3. Search for duplicate issues.
  4. Read the approved brief.
  5. Report permission or context uncertainty.

docs.title: Decide what to do with existing work
docs.text:
Candidate Decision Exact duplicate Reuse or close according to repository policy Partial overlap Extend the existing issue and create only the missing work Conflict Keep separate and record why Unrelated Leave unchanged

The lab includes open, closed, overlapping, and conflicting status issues.

docs.title: Decompose by outcome
docs.text:
Create one parent issue and child issues with defined scope.

Each child needs:

  • an independently reviewable result;
  • results needed for acceptance;
  • a non-goal;
  • dependencies;
  • an owner or visible ownership gap.

docs.title: Preview the complete write
docs.text:
Before approval, show:

  • repository owner and name;
  • issue count;
  • every title and body;
  • labels and milestone;
  • relationships;
  • fields left unset.

docs.title: People approve the operation
docs.text:
Copilot proposes the action.

Record Approve, Revise, or Reject before the write.

No approval, no issues.

docs.title: Check what GitHub saved
docs.text:
After the write:

  1. start a fresh request;
  2. retrieve the issues;
  3. compare them with the approved plan;
  4. correct one defect;
  5. retrieve the corrected issue again.

docs.title: Lab result
docs.text:
• Temporary reviewed issue preview
  • Authoritative live issue set
  • One parent issue
  • Four required child roles; an optional fifth stays outside Session M7-05
  • Saved issues checked through a fresh GitHub read
  • Parent-to-child links that Session M7-04 reads directly

Stop if you cannot review the tool call or check the saved issues.

docs.title: Lab
docs.text: Overview Lab Trainer Guide

docs.title: Session M7-03 lab: Create, check, and correct a GitHub issue plan
docs.text:
Duration: 2 hours

Difficulty: Intermediate

docs.title: Lab outcome
docs.text:
Create a reviewed GitHub issue hierarchy through MCP. Read the issues back to check what was saved. Make one focused correction and read it back again. You end with live parent and child issues and the corrected issue.

Part Work Time 1 Check GitHub MCP and write access 15 min 2 Read the source and existing GitHub state 20 min 3 Design and review the issue hierarchy 30 min 4 Preview and create the issues 35 min 5 Check and correct one issue 20 min

docs.title: Before you start
docs.text: Complete the track capability setup.

docs.title: Part 1: Check GitHub MCP and write access (15 minutes)
docs.text:
In the GitHub Copilot app:

  1. open Customize → MCP → Installed;
  2. check that the approved GitHub MCP connection is available;
  3. start a session for the training repository;
  4. ask Copilot to list the GitHub tools it can use;
  5. ask it to retrieve the repository name and five open issues;
  6. check that you have issue-write permission.

GitHub MCP is built into Copilot CLI. CLI users can inspect it with:

/mcp list
/mcp show github

If the connection is missing, use Customize → MCP to install or configure the GitHub server. Never paste a token into a prompt or repository file.

docs.title: Part 2: Read the source and existing GitHub state (20 minutes)
docs.text:
Attach the approved Session M7-02 decision brief and issue proposal. Use starter/approved-decision-brief.md when those artifacts are unavailable.

Ask Copilot to:

  1. summarize the approved outcome, non-goals, results needed for acceptance, and owners;
  2. retrieve available labels and milestones;
  3. read starter/existing-issues.json, then search open and closed issues for matching live work;
  4. report every GitHub MCP read it used;
  5. identify any decision in the proposal that is absent from the brief.

Classify each candidate as duplicate, partial overlap, conflict, or unrelated. Record what you will do with it and why in the issue plan.

Checkpoint: No issue is proposed until the source and existing repository state have both been read.

docs.title: Part 3: Design and review the issue hierarchy (30 minutes)
docs.text:
Copy starter/issue-plan-template.md into your working folder.

This file is a temporary preview. Don't commit it. The live issues replace it.

Ask Copilot to propose:

  • one parent issue for the approved outcome;
  • four child issues: public status mapping, requester status view, empty and stale states, and requester-access verification;
  • dependencies and parallel work;
  • acceptance criteria and non-goals;
  • source links to the decision brief;
  • ownership gaps left unassigned.

Review the plan before any write.

These four roles feed Sessions M7-04 and M7-05. A fifth issue is optional and stays outside the four orchestration workstreams.

Reuse or update an existing issue when it owns part of the approved outcome. Link a closed duplicate for context. Do not merge conflicting or out-of-scope work.

Reject or revise an issue that:

  • combines unrelated outcomes;
  • duplicates existing work;
  • gives reviewers no way to check acceptance;
  • invents an assignee, label, milestone, or date;
  • includes work excluded by the decision brief.

Checkpoint: Every child issue traces to a decision and can be reviewed independently.

docs.title: Part 4: Preview and create the issues (30 minutes)
docs.text:
Send:

Before using a GitHub write tool, show the repository owner and name, issue count,
full title and body for every issue, labels, milestone, parent-child references,
dependencies, and every field left unset. Wait for my approval.

Compare the preview with the issue plan. Revise it until it is safe to approve.

After approval, ask Copilot to create the issues through GitHub MCP. Save each returned issue number and URL in the parent issue or its linked child issues.

Checkpoint: The live hierarchy contains one parent and the four required child roles in the approved repository. Reuse existing issues that cover a required role. The hierarchy may also contain one optional fifth child.

docs.title: Part 5: Check and correct one issue (15 minutes)
docs.text:
Start a new Copilot request. Don't reuse the create response.

Ask Copilot to retrieve the created issues through GitHub MCP. Compare the saved issues with the approved plan:

  • title and body;
  • acceptance criteria and non-goals;
  • labels and milestone;
  • source links and relationships;
  • ownership fields.

Choose one child issue and add the missing section that names who will check the work and which decision it follows:

Verification owner: Delivery reviewer
Source decision: docs/discovery/decision-brief.md

Require a full update preview. Approve the focused write, then retrieve the issue again and check the new section is present.

Checkpoint: Fresh reads show that GitHub saved both the issues and the correction.

Link every child issue from the parent. Mark the four required roles and label any optional fifth child as outside the Session M7-05 workstreams. Record dependency order, unresolved ownership, your decisions about existing work, and the correction you checked. Session M7-04 reads this live issue set through GitHub MCP.

docs.title: Trainer Guide
docs.text: Overview Lab Trainer Guide

docs.title: Session M7-03 trainer guide: Plan work with GitHub Issues and MCP
docs.text: 00:00 Start timer Reset timer Print guide      Enable timer shortcut (T)

docs.title: Goal
docs.text: Show learners how to plan a GitHub MCP write, approve it, and check what GitHub stored. Once created, the live issues become the source of record.

docs.title: One-hour plan
docs.text: Time Segment 0:00-0:08 Connect the decision brief to saved GitHub issues 0:08-0:18 Explain MCP from the learner's point of view 0:18-0:30 Inspect tools, permissions, and repository context 0:30-0:43 Decompose the initiative into an issue plan 0:43-0:53 Preview, approve, and check a write 0:53-1:00 Explain the lab guardrails

docs.title: Prepare
docs.text:
• Every learner can open the GitHub Copilot app.
  • The GitHub MCP server is available: Customize → MCP → Installed.
  • Test one GitHub read before demonstrating a write.
  • Learners can read the training repository and create issues in it. Use a training repository, not a production backlog.
  • Note the repository owner and name.

Stop if a learner can't identify the target repository, inspect the tool call, or check the resulting issue.

docs.title: Explain MCP without implementation detail
docs.text:
An MCP server gives Copilot a set of named tools for reading or changing another system.

  • The tool runs with the permissions of the connection.
  • A read can still expose restricted information.
  • A write must name its target and proposed values.
  • Copilot proposes an action. The learner approves it.
  • Check the saved result with a new read. Copilot's success message isn't enough.

Skip server protocols, transports, and SDKs.

docs.title: 1. Read the source
docs.text: Open lab/starter/approved-decision-brief.md. Ask Copilot for the outcome, constraints, non-goals, owners, and results needed for acceptance.

docs.title: 2. Inspect GitHub
docs.text:
Ask Copilot to identify the target repository, list relevant labels, and search for duplicate or overlapping open issues.

Use lab/starter/existing-issues.json when the training repository lacks the seeded records. Have learners decide what to do with each candidate:

  • reuse #241: it partially overlaps the requester view;
  • leave #256 unchanged: notifications are out of scope;
  • reject #263: it is implementation work that conflicts with the visibility boundary;
  • link #278 only as historical context.

docs.title: 3. Propose the issue set
docs.text:
Use one parent issue and four child roles: public status mapping, requester status view, empty and stale states, and requester-access verification. These feed Sessions M7-04 and M7-05. A fifth child is optional and stays outside those four workstreams. Each issue needs:

  • a clear outcome;
  • scope and a non-goal;
  • acceptance criteria;
  • dependencies;
  • owner or ownership gap;
  • link to the decision brief.

Reject technical subtasks with no independent outcome or review point. The Markdown plan is a temporary preview. Don't commit it or hand it to the next session.

docs.title: 4. Preview the write
docs.text:
Before Copilot calls a write tool, it shows:

  • repository owner and name;
  • issue count;
  • each title and body;
  • labels and milestone;
  • parent-child relationship method;
  • fields left unset.

The learner records Approve, Revise, or Reject.

docs.title: 5. Check and correct
docs.text:
After creation, retrieve the issues in a fresh read and compare them with the plan. Demonstrate a correction: add the verification owner and source-decision path to one child issue. Preview the update, approve it, write it, and read it back.

Check that the parent issue links the complete child set. Session M7-04 reads those issues directly.

docs.title: Common failures
docs.text: Failure Response Copilot targets the wrong repository Reject the operation and restate the repository Duplicate issue exists Link or update it instead of creating another Partial overlap exists Reuse the covered work and create only the missing outcomes Child issue is too broad Split it before the write Labels don't exist Use existing labels or leave the field unset Tool output claims success without a returned issue Run a fresh repository read
