docs.title: Session M7-04: Build and use a planning canvas
docs.text:
Open slides Slides in new tab Download PDF Close slides

Module: Product and Delivery Teams

Difficulty: Intermediate

Prerequisites: Sessions M7-01 to M7-03, GitHub Copilot app access, GitHub MCP access, and canvas creation access

Duration: 3 hours (1 hour trainer content + 2 hours lab)

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
Continue the Delivery Decision Studio path. Use the built-in /create-canvas skill to turn the live Session M7-03 issues into a visible delivery workspace. Review the generated extension and remove capabilities you do not need. Then change GitHub state and compare it with the canvas. Detect the stale data and refresh it. You describe and operate the canvas without hand-coding the extension.

Important

You need /create-canvas, GitHub MCP, and canvas creation access.

docs.title: Learning outcomes
docs.text:
In this session, you will:

  1. Decide when a canvas is more useful than another chat response.
  2. Describe the state and actions needed for a planning canvas.
  3. Create a canvas from a plain-language request.
  4. Review and simplify the generated capabilities.
  5. Load approved GitHub issues into the canvas.
  6. Detect drift between visible canvas state and a fresh GitHub read.
  7. Refresh and reconcile the canvas.
  8. Record ownership, refresh, recovery, and retirement conditions.
  9. Leave a live canvas linked to the GitHub issues for Session M7-05.

docs.title: Session structure
docs.text: Block Duration Material Trainer content 1 hour Trainer guide Lab 2 hours Lab guide

docs.title: Materials
docs.text: Resource Location Slides slides.md Canvas requirements lab/starter/

docs.title: Session M3-01 distinction
docs.text: Session M3-01 teaches canvas extension design and implementation. Session M7-04 teaches you to request, review, and operate a canvas through the GitHub Copilot app.

docs.title: Build and use a planning canvas
docs.text: Session M7-04 | Product and Delivery Teams | Intermediate

docs.title: Use visible state when chat stops being enough
docs.text:
A canvas helps you review several records and make repeated updates through named actions. Keep that view available after the conversation ends.

The source is the live Session M7-03 parent issue and its linked child issues, not the previous chat.

docs.title: Keep GitHub state and planning information distinct
docs.text:
GitHub records issue state. The canvas groups that state with planning information that helps people decide what to do next.

GitHub fact Canvas planning view Open issue Ready for discovery Assigned issue Ownership confirmed Blocked issue Risk, dependency, and next decision Closed issue Planning result recorded

Label the two kinds of state differently. Otherwise the team cannot tell whether they are seeing a decision or a source-system fact.

docs.title: Keep fields that change a decision
docs.text:
Field Keep it when Remove it when Risk It changes sequencing or approval It only repeats the issue body Owner The responsible person is unclear GitHub already makes it clear Next action A team needs a follow-up It is only a status synonym

The canvas should expose important work without becoming a second backlog.

docs.title: Review canvas updates
docs.text:
Observe source state
      ↓
Propose canvas update
      ↓
Review the affected record
      ↓
Accept, revise, or reject

Use this loop to catch stale data and updates that lack supporting sources.

docs.title: Start from live GitHub issues
docs.text:
The canvas should show:

  • parent objective;
  • issue and planning status;
  • owner or ownership gap;
  • dependency and risk;
  • decision and next action.

docs.title: Create it in plain language
docs.text:
/create-canvas Create a delivery-planning canvas for the approved GitHub issues.
People can update planning status and record decisions. Copilot can summarize
and propose updates. Do not close issues, change assignees, or publish content.

This is a no-code review. Inspect generated files and capabilities, then ask Copilot for specific changes.

docs.title: Review before use
docs.text:
Ask:

  1. Does each field support a real decision?
  2. Can every action be explained?
  3. Are external writes excluded?
  4. Can the owner recover?
  5. When should the canvas be retired?

docs.title: Simpler is better
docs.text: Remove generated fields and actions that do not help the team decide or act.

docs.title: Load live GitHub issues
docs.text:
Use GitHub MCP to retrieve the Session M7-03 issues.

Copilot can move the approved fields into the canvas. GitHub remains the source for issue state.

docs.title: Label planning state separately
docs.text:
The canvas may show ready for review while the GitHub issue remains open.

That is acceptable when the canvas labels the planning state and source-system state separately.

docs.title: Check three views
docs.text:
Compare:

  • the visible canvas;
  • Copilot's report;
  • a fresh GitHub MCP read.

Resolve or explain every mismatch.

docs.title: Create visible drift
docs.text:
1. Preview and approve a GitHub issue comment through MCP.
  2. Retrieve the changed issue in a fresh request.
  3. Do not refresh the canvas.
  4. Compare the new GitHub state with the visible canvas.

The canvas should show that its last refresh is older than the source change.

docs.title: Refresh the canvas
docs.text:
Use the approved refresh capability.

Check:

  • the blocker appears in planning state;
  • the next action names the owner decision;
  • GitHub state and planning state stay distinct;
  • the last-refresh time changes.

docs.title: Critique the live state
docs.text:
Run /context, then use a fresh session when needed.

Ask /rubber-duck to find stale claims, mixed state labels, unsafe actions, and missing owners.

The live canvas and linked issues are authoritative for Session M7-05.

docs.title: Lab result
docs.text:
• Learner-created canvas
  • Reviewed state and actions
  • Live GitHub issue data
  • A detected and reconciled state mismatch
  • Owner, refresh, recovery, and retirement rules
  • Four linked status-visibility workstream candidates

docs.title: Lab
docs.text: Overview Lab Trainer Guide

docs.title: Session M7-04 lab: Build a planning canvas and reconcile stale state
docs.text:
Duration: 2 hours

Difficulty: Intermediate

docs.title: Lab outcome
docs.text:
Create and review a planning canvas with the built-in /create-canvas skill. Load live issue state through GitHub MCP. Change an issue in GitHub, detect the stale canvas data, and refresh it. You end with a project-scoped canvas linked to the live issues.

Part Work Time 1 Check canvas and MCP capabilities 15 min 2 Define the minimum canvas requirements 20 min 3 Create and simplify the canvas 30 min 4 Load and operate live issue state 25 min 5 Create and detect state drift 15 min 6 Reconcile and record ownership 15 min

docs.title: Before you start
docs.text: Complete the track capability setup.

docs.title: Part 1: Check canvas and MCP capabilities (15 minutes)
docs.text:
1. Open a GitHub Copilot app session for the training repository.
  2. Type / and check that /create-canvas appears.
  3. Open Customize → Canvas and inspect installed canvases.
  4. Open Customize → MCP → Installed and check GitHub MCP.
  5. Ask Copilot to retrieve the Session M7-03 parent issue and child issues.

/create-canvas is a built-in app skill. Don't install a community replacement.

Use a fresh GitHub MCP read as the authoritative issue list. Start from the live Session M7-03 parent issue and follow its child links, not chat history.

docs.title: Part 2: Define the minimum canvas requirements (20 minutes)
docs.text:
Complete starter/canvas-requirements.md.

The canvas must answer:

  • What outcome are we delivering?
  • Which issues are planned, active, blocked, or ready for review?
  • Who owns the next action?
  • Which dependency or risk needs attention?
  • When did GitHub state last refresh?

Allow only these actions:

  • refresh issue state from GitHub;
  • change planning status in the canvas;
  • record a risk or decision;
  • assign the next planning action.

The canvas must not close issues, change assignees, or publish comments.

Checkpoint: Every field and action supports a named planning decision.

docs.title: Part 3: Create and simplify the canvas (30 minutes)
docs.text:
Run:

/create-canvas

Create a project-scoped delivery-planning canvas from
@starter/canvas-requirements.md. Store it under .github/extensions. It must show
the parent outcome, child issues, planning status, GitHub state, owner, dependency,
risk, next action, and last refresh. It may read GitHub state but must not write
to GitHub.

The agent should create the extension and open it in the side panel.

Review:

  • the files created under .github/extensions;
  • the visible fields and actions;
  • the capabilities exposed to Copilot;
  • any package or dependency added by the extension.

Inspect the generated files and ask Copilot for specific changes. Don't hand-edit extension code.

Ask Copilot to remove generated state or actions that exceed the requirements.

Checkpoint: The canvas is smaller after review and contains no GitHub write action.

docs.title: Part 4: Load and operate live issue state (25 minutes)
docs.text:
Ask Copilot to retrieve the Session M7-03 issues through GitHub MCP and load:

  • issue number and title;
  • GitHub state;
  • planning status;
  • owner or ownership gap;
  • dependency;
  • next action;
  • retrieval time.

Then:

  1. change one planning status through the visible canvas controls;
  2. ask Copilot to change another planning status through a canvas capability;
  3. add one risk with an owner;
  4. add one decision with a reason;
  5. ask Copilot for a current canvas summary.

Compare the visible state with Copilot's summary.

docs.title: Part 5: Create and detect state drift (15 minutes)
docs.text:
Choose one child issue. Through GitHub MCP, preview this comment:

Planning update: waiting for a product-owner decision on the public status
vocabulary. Do not start implementation until the decision brief is updated.

Approve the comment, then retrieve the issue in a fresh request.

Do not refresh the canvas yet. Ask Copilot to compare:

  • the current visible canvas;
  • the fresh GitHub issue;
  • the canvas's last-refresh time.

Identify what changed in GitHub but has not yet appeared in the canvas.

docs.title: Part 6: Reconcile and record ownership (15 minutes)
docs.text:
Use the canvas refresh action or ask Copilot to call the approved refresh capability.

Check that:

  • the issue's planning status reflects the new blocker;
  • the next action names the product-owner decision;
  • the GitHub state and planning state remain distinct;
  • the last-refresh time changed.

In the live canvas, record who owns it, how to refresh it, and how to recover after an interruption. Also record when to retire it and the next safe action. Check that it links the four status-visibility issues for Session M7-05. Keep any optional fifth issue linked for context, but outside those workstreams.

Run /context. If the creation thread is crowded, start a fresh session and retrieve the live GitHub issues and open the canvas. Then run:

/rubber-duck Critique the live planning canvas against the linked GitHub issues.
Find stale source claims, mixed GitHub and planning states, unsafe actions, and
missing ownership.

Apply useful findings directly to the canvas.

docs.title: Trainer Guide
docs.text: Overview Lab Trainer Guide

docs.title: Session M7-04 trainer guide: Build and use a planning canvas
docs.text:
00:00 Start timer Reset timer Print guide Enable timer shortcut (T)

Duration: 1 hour

docs.title: Goal
docs.text: Show learners how to create and review a project-scoped planning canvas. The canvas displays GitHub state alongside planning information. GitHub remains the source of record.

docs.title: One-hour plan
docs.text: Time Segment 0:00-0:08 Decide when visible state helps 0:08-0:18 Translate live issues into canvas requirements 0:18-0:32 Create the canvas with /create-canvas 0:32-0:43 Review state, actions, and boundaries 0:43-0:53 Create drift and reconcile the canvas 0:53-1:00 Explain ownership and launch the lab

docs.title: Prepare
docs.text:
• Every learner has the GitHub Copilot app with /create-canvas. Show it under Customize → Skills → Installed as a built-in skill.
  • Learners can read the Session M7-03 parent and child issues through GitHub MCP.
  • Use a training repository and synthetic issue data.
  • Name the canvas owner and reviewer.
  • /context, /clear or /reset, and /rubber-duck work.

A static JSON edit doesn't meet this session's outcome. It needs live canvas creation.

docs.title: When to use a canvas
docs.text:
Use a canvas when work needs:

  • visible shared state;
  • repeated updates;
  • several related records;
  • named actions;
  • a view people can review after the chat ends.

Keep a single answer, draft, or short interview in chat.

docs.title: Translate the plan into requirements
docs.text:
Start from lab/starter/canvas-requirements.md. The minimum planning state is:

  • parent objective;
  • issue number and title;
  • status;
  • owner or ownership gap;
  • dependency;
  • risk;
  • decision;
  • next action.

The source set is fixed: public status mapping, requester status view, empty and stale states, and access-boundary verification.

The minimum actions are:

  • load or refresh approved GitHub issues;
  • change a planning status;
  • record a decision;
  • add or update a risk;
  • produce a current summary.

Closing issues, changing assignees, or publishing updates stays outside the canvas.

docs.title: Demonstration prompt
docs.text:
/create-canvas Create a delivery-planning canvas for the approved GitHub issues.
Show the parent objective, issue number, status, owner, dependency, risk,
decision, and next action. People can update planning status and record
decisions. Copilot can summarize the canvas and propose updates. Do not close
issues, change assignees, or publish content without a separate confirmation.

After generation, ask learners what they would remove. Keep only what supports a decision or action.

docs.title: Review the generated canvas
docs.text:
Check:

  1. Does every state field support a real decision?
  2. Can each action be explained in one sentence?
  3. Does the canvas distinguish planning state from GitHub issue state?
  4. Are external writes excluded or separately approved?
  5. Can the owner recover after an interrupted update?
  6. Is there a clear reason to retire the canvas?

docs.title: Demo update and drift
docs.text:
1. Ask Copilot to retrieve the Session M7-03 issues through GitHub MCP.
  2. Load the approved issue fields into the canvas.
  3. Change one status through the visible controls.
  4. Ask Copilot to record one decision.
  5. Add the lab's reviewed blocker comment to one GitHub issue through MCP.
  6. Read the issue again without refreshing the canvas.
  7. Show the mismatch and last-refresh time.
  8. Refresh the canvas and check the blocker and next action.

Leave learners with the live canvas and linked GitHub issues, not a transfer file.

docs.title: Session M7-05: Orchestrate agents and workstreams
docs.text:
Open slides Slides in new tab Download PDF Close slides

Module: Product and Delivery Teams

Difficulty: Intermediate

Prerequisites: Live GitHub Copilot app orchestration access; Sessions M7-01 to M7-04 for the product route, or Sessions M1-01 to M1-03, M2-01 to M2-04 and M2-05 for the developer route

Duration: 3 hours (1 hour trainer content + 2 hours lab)

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
Use parent-led orchestration for one delivery objective. Split four live GitHub issues into independent workstreams, then monitor the child sessions and review their results.

On the developer route after Session M2-05, you review a local readiness evaluator, its tests, and a synthetic PR snapshot instead. You don't need GitHub MCP or product-track artifacts. Both routes use the same two-hour lab.

Each workstream needs a question, input paths or issues, a stop condition, and a reviewer. GitHub Copilot keeps session status, links, timing, and usage on the orchestration surface.

Live orchestration is required. There is no role-play or prepared-result route.

docs.title: Learning objectives
docs.text:
You will:

  1. Split one objective into independent workstreams.
  2. Set inputs and hard stop conditions.
  3. Start and monitor child sessions through /orchestrate.
  4. Redirect, stop, accept, or reject work.
  5. Return a reviewed parent result backed by the route's sources.
  6. Separate local test success from PR readiness (developer route).

docs.title: Session M5-01 distinction
docs.text: Session M5-01 uses an optional framework for persistent roles and routing. Session M7-05 uses built-in orchestration for temporary workstreams. The parent reviews every result and keeps decision authority.

docs.title: Materials
docs.text: Resource Location Trainer guide trainer-content/README.md Slides slides.md Lab guide lab/README.md Learner assets lab/starter/ Reference solution lab/solution/

docs.title: You need
docs.text: The built-in orchestrate skill and /orchestrate command in the GitHub Copilot app. Product learners also need GitHub MCP read access to their parent and child issues. Developers need Python 3.10 or later and local project read access.

docs.title: References
docs.text:
• Built-in skills for the GitHub Copilot app
  • Slash commands for the GitHub Copilot app
  • Working with agent sessions in the GitHub Copilot app
  • Managing agent sessions

docs.title: Product and delivery teams, or developers after Session M2-05
docs.text: Session M7-05 | 3 hours

docs.title: Agenda
docs.text: Segment Time Parent objective and boundaries 10 min Minimal workstream plan 10 min Monitor and intervene 12 min Live demonstration 13 min Review and lab handoff 15 min

docs.title: Required access
docs.text:
• /orchestrate creates and coordinates live child sessions.
  • Product route: GitHub MCP reads the selected issues.
  • Developer route: local project read access and Python 3.10 or later.
  • You can open, redirect, and stop child sessions.

docs.title: Choose one lab route
docs.text:
Route Inputs Result Product and delivery Four live GitHub issues Parent result used by Session M7-06 Developer Local evaluator, tests, synthetic PR snapshot Separate implementation, coverage, and PR conclusions

Each route takes 120 minutes. Developers need Session M2-05, not Sessions M7-01 to M7-04.

docs.title: One parent objective
docs.text:
Review the four approved status-visibility issues and return one reviewed result for each.

The parent owns scope and review.

docs.title: Keep the plan small
docs.text:
Each workstream needs:

  • a question with a clear scope;
  • approved inputs;
  • a stop condition;
  • a reviewer.

The orchestration surface already holds session links, status, timing, and usage.

docs.title: Four independent workstreams
docs.text:
Workstream Question Public mapping Is the mapping ready for approval? Requester status Is the issue ready for implementation review? Empty and stale states Are fallback states testable? Access boundary Are the approved requester-access results ready?

Move shared questions back to the parent.

docs.title: Developer workstreams
docs.text:
Question Input Does implementation meet the behavior contract? Brief and evaluator What do tests prove or miss? Brief, tests, and evaluator Is the supplied PR ready? Brief and PR snapshot

Children read the same fixed inputs. They do not wait for one another or edit.

docs.title: Practise steering
docs.text:
Redirect the test reviewer after its first answer:

Check criterion 5. Does the test prove sorted reason codes, the exact complete
reason list, or both? Do not edit files.

Inspect the revised answer. A follow-up doesn't prove the first answer was wrong.

docs.title: Reconcile the readiness claim
docs.text:
The synthetic author says: "Local tests pass, so the PR is READY."

Check the actual snapshot:

  • required integration-tests failed;
  • blocking thread R1 is unresolved.

Check the parent's decision against the snapshot. Local success doesn't override PR blockers.

docs.title: Start live orchestration
docs.text:
/orchestrate Use the four workstreams in my approved plan. Keep them independent.
Each result must answer its question, cite approved inputs, state unresolved
gaps, and give a recommendation. Obey each stop condition.

docs.title: Monitor on the platform
docs.text: Signal Action Safe and on scope Wait Safe work needs correction Redirect A boundary is crossed Stop The result meets the plan Accept The result lacks support Reject Human authority is required Escalate

docs.title: Review each result
docs.text:
• Does it answer the assigned question?
  • Does it use only the approved issues and their linked sources?
  • Did it obey the stop condition?
  • Are gaps listed?
  • Is the recommendation supported?

Reject answers that lack supporting sources.

docs.title: The parent result is the handoff
docs.text:
The reviewed result:

  • links findings to live GitHub issues;
  • shows rejected claims;
  • names gaps and owners;
  • recommends the next follow-up.

Session M7-06 reads this result and the live issues.

docs.title: The human keeps authority
docs.text: Copilot coordinates work. A person reviews results and approves any issue update, publication, or release statement.

docs.title: Session M5-01 is different
docs.text: Session M5-01 Session M7-05 Persistent roles and routing Temporary workstreams Optional framework setup Built-in orchestration Shared memory Live issues and their supporting sources

docs.title: Lab deliverable
docs.text:
1. Approved orchestration plan
  2. Live child-session results
  3. Reviewed parent result linked to live issues

Keep progress on the orchestration surface, not in a status form.

For developers, use the developer plan and reviewed parent result instead of live issues. Include the actual redirection, rejected or unresolved claims, and observed usage.

docs.title: Lab
docs.text: Overview Lab Trainer Guide

docs.title: Session M7-05 lab: Orchestrate agents and workstreams
docs.text:
Duration: 2 hours

Difficulty: Intermediate

Prerequisites: Live app orchestration access; Sessions M7-01 to M7-04 and GitHub MCP read access for the product route, or Sessions M1-01 to M1-03, M2-01 to M2-04 and M2-05 for the developer route

docs.title: Choose one route
docs.text:
Both routes use the built-in /orchestrate skill and live child sessions. Separate prompts and prepared answers don't complete the lab.

Route Use after Inputs Lab time Product and delivery Sessions M7-01 to M7-04 Live GitHub issues through MCP 120 min Developer Sessions M1-01 to M1-03, M2-01 to M2-04 and M2-05 Local Python code and a synthetic PR snapshot 120 min

Complete one route. Developers don't need GitHub issues, canvases, or MCP.

docs.title: Scenario
docs.text:
You work with four live GitHub issues: public status mapping, requester status, empty and stale states, and requester access. Orchestrate one workstream per issue. Session M7-06 uses your reviewed parent result.

Select the four required roles from the parent issue's child links. Any optional fifth child stays outside this orchestration.

docs.title: Before you start
docs.text:
• /orchestrate is available.
  • GitHub MCP can retrieve the parent and child issues.
  • You can open, redirect, and stop child sessions.
  • Stop any work that requests production data, personal data, secrets, external contact, publication, or unapproved changes.

docs.title: Schedule
docs.text: Exercise Work Time 1 Approve and start the plan 30 min 2 Monitor and intervene 35 min 3 Review results 35 min 4 Return the parent result 20 min

docs.title: Exercise 1: Approve and start the plan
docs.text:
Open starter/orchestration-plan-template.md.

  1. Retrieve the approved parent and child issues through GitHub MCP.
  2. Define one question with a clear scope for each child issue.
  3. Name the approved issue and its linked sources for each workstream.
  4. Add a hard stop condition and reviewer.
  5. Check that no child depends on another child result.
  6. Submit the plan through /orchestrate.

Use this prompt:

/orchestrate Use the four workstreams in my approved plan. Keep them independent.
Each result must answer its assigned question, cite its approved inputs, state
unresolved gaps, and give a recommendation. Obey each stop condition. Do not
publish, contact people, access restricted data, or change systems.

Open each child session from the orchestration surface. Check its question, inputs, stop condition, and reviewer.

docs.title: Exercise 2: Monitor and intervene
docs.text:
Use the orchestration surface as the live record. Don't copy session identifiers, status, timing, or usage into the plan.

Signal Action Safe and on scope Wait A safe result needs a precise correction Redirect A boundary is crossed Stop The result's answer is supported by its sources Accept The result is unsupported or outside scope Reject Human authority is required Escalate

Redirect only when the child can safely fix a specific problem with scope or supporting sources.

docs.title: Exercise 3: Review results
docs.text:
Review each child result against its workstream:

  • Does it answer the assigned question?
  • Does it use only the approved issue and its linked sources?
  • Did it obey the stop condition?
  • Are unresolved gaps listed?
  • Is the recommendation supported?

Reject unsupported claims. Redirect a safe, repairable result. Stop work that crosses a hard boundary.

docs.title: Exercise 4: Return the parent result
docs.text:
Ask the parent to summarize only the reviewed child results.

The parent result must:

  • link each finding to its GitHub issue;
  • separate accepted findings from rejected claims;
  • name unresolved gaps and their owners;
  • state which issues are ready for follow-up;
  • avoid publication or source-system changes.

Add the reviewed result to the parent GitHub issue if the trainer allows that write. Retrieve the issue again to check the update.

Session M7-06 uses the live GitHub issues and this parent result.

docs.title: Completion check
docs.text:
• Plan with four workstreams, each with a defined scope.
  • Live child results on the orchestration surface.
  • At least one deliberate wait, redirect, stop, accept, or reject decision.
  • Reviewed parent result linked to the live GitHub issues.
  • Any issue update checked through a fresh GitHub read.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text: Issue Response A child requests restricted data Stop the child and record the boundary in the parent result. A result cites no supporting issue content Reject it or redirect the child. Two workstreams overlap Pause one and move the shared question to the parent. An issue cannot be retrieved Stop that workstream until approved issue access is restored.

docs.title: Goal and access
docs.text:
Supervise independent read-only reviews of a readiness evaluator, its tests, and a supplied PR snapshot. Passing local tests and PR readiness are different claims.

You need the GitHub Copilot app with /orchestrate, local project read access, and Python 3.10 or later. No GitHub connection, MCP server, or remote write is needed.

docs.title: Prepare the local project
docs.text:
From the curriculum root, copy these files to a fresh workspace:

mkdir -p ~/copilot-labs/session-m7-05-developer
cp -R sessions/session-m2-05-copilot-app-for-developers/lab/solution/readiness_guard \
  ~/copilot-labs/session-m7-05-developer/
cp -R sessions/session-m2-05-copilot-app-for-developers/lab/solution/tests \
  ~/copilot-labs/session-m7-05-developer/
cp sessions/session-m2-05-copilot-app-for-developers/lab/starter/issue-brief.md \
  ~/copilot-labs/session-m7-05-developer/
cp sessions/session-m2-05-copilot-app-for-developers/lab/starter/prepared-evidence/05-pr-snapshot.json \
  ~/copilot-labs/session-m7-05-developer/pr-snapshot.json
cp sessions/session-m7-05-orchestrate-workstreams/lab/starter/developer-review-brief.md \
  sessions/session-m7-05-orchestrate-workstreams/lab/starter/developer-orchestration-plan.md \
  ~/copilot-labs/session-m7-05-developer/
cd ~/copilot-labs/session-m7-05-developer
PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 python -m unittest discover -s tests -v

The supplied reference implementation's six tests should pass. You review the implementation; don't repair it or install packages. Attach this folder as an app project. Keep the children read-only and restrict tool access to the named files and test command. Grant no network or GitHub write access.

docs.title: Exercise D1: Accept the work split (25 minutes)
docs.text:
Read developer-review-brief.md and complete developer-orchestration-plan.md.

Use independent questions:

Workstream Question Inputs Implementation Does the evaluator meet the brief's behavior contract? issue-brief.md, readiness_guard/ Tests What do the tests prove, and what remains untested? issue-brief.md, tests/, readiness_guard/ PR state Is the supplied PR ready based on its required checks and threads? issue-brief.md, pr-snapshot.json

Each child works from its own inputs and does not wait for another child. The parent compares the results afterward. Name a reviewer and set stop conditions and a usage limit. The test reviewer may run only the supplied test command.

docs.title: Exercise D2: Start and inspect live work (30 minutes)
docs.text:
Submit the accepted plan:

/orchestrate Use developer-orchestration-plan.md to start independent read-only
reviews of implementation, tests, and PR state. Each child must answer its
question, cite files or JSON fields, and state uncertainty. Keep scope limited to
the named local files and test command. Do not edit, install, use the network, or
change GitHub. Stop at the agreed usage limit. The parent alone reconciles results.

Open the live children and check their inputs and task boundaries. Do not substitute /fleet, separate chats, or captured answers.

docs.title: Exercise D3: Redirect and reconcile (35 minutes)
docs.text:
After the test reviewer returns its first result, redirect that child:

Check your test-coverage conclusion against acceptance criterion 5 in
issue-brief.md. Explain whether sorted reason codes are tested and whether the
test also proves the exact complete reason list. Do not edit or broaden the task.

Compare the child's original and revised answers. The redirect is a planned follow-up, not proof that the first answer was wrong. Stop a child if it crosses scope; don't stage a harmful action to demonstrate stopping.

Then ask the parent to reconcile all results with the provisional READY note in developer-review-brief.md. Check any disagreement against the source files. If children agree, say so.

docs.title: Exercise D4: Review the parent result (30 minutes)
docs.text:
Require the parent to return:

  • a separate verdict for implementation behavior, test coverage, and PR readiness;
  • accepted findings with file or JSON-field references;
  • rejected or unresolved claims and the reason;
  • the effect of the child redirection;
  • remaining gaps and the next human decision.

Check that the parent explains why passing local tests cannot override a failed required PR check or unresolved blocking thread. Review the result yourself and keep it in the app session. Inspect the app's usage display and explain whether orchestration was worth using for this work.

docs.title: Developer completion check
docs.text:
• Plan with independent questions and a usage limit.
  • Live child sessions inspected on the orchestration surface.
  • Test reviewer redirected and its revised answer checked.
  • Provisional READY note accepted or rejected using the actual PR fields.
  • Parent result separates implementation, test coverage, and PR state.
  • No source files, packages, or external systems changed.
  • A human decision and observed usage are recorded in the parent result.

Compare your result with solution/developer-review-reference.md. That reference can't replace live child-session work.

docs.title: Trainer supplement: Orchestrate work tracked in Azure Boards
docs.text:
Time: 45 to 60 minutes inside the existing two-hour lab

Use: Azure Boards is the issue source for the main lab.

Important

The trainer selects and prepares this route before the workshop. It isn't part of the standard learner path.

Use a seeded Azure Boards Epic or Feature for the same four Session M7-03 issue roles. Keep the plan and status in Azure Boards, and repository work in GitHub.

GitHub Copilot performs the orchestration. Azure Boards MCP and the browser are planning interfaces. They don't replace the built-in /orchestrate skill.

docs.title: Prepare
docs.text:
You need:

  • a training Azure DevOps project with the seeded status-visibility Epic or Feature;
  • permission to read and update the seeded child work items;
  • an Azure Boards MCP connection or browser access;
  • the work item IDs or seed tag from the trainer;
  • /orchestrate in the GitHub Copilot app;
  • the fictional GitHub repository when a selected item needs repository evidence.

Before starting:

  1. Open the seeded parent and check it is tagged for Session M7-05 training.
  2. Record the parent ID, process type, starting state, and selected child IDs.
  3. Check /orchestrate appears and the built-in orchestrate skill is under Customize → Skills → Installed.
  4. Check you can open, steer, and stop child sessions.
  5. Name who reviews the parent result and who approves Boards updates.

Separate prompts, role-play, exports, and prepared results don't replace the live run. Use only the seeded fictional items.

docs.title: Parent objective
docs.text:
Use the seeded status-visibility Epic or Feature.

Review the four approved status-visibility items and return one reviewed result for each. Do not change production systems or publish claims.

docs.title: Step 1: Select independent child work items
docs.text:
Open the parent item through approved MCP tools or the browser. Select up to four children. Give each a separate question and approved inputs.

Mirror the standard lab wording:

Session M7-03 issue role Azure Boards child wording Public status mapping Public status mapping approval Requester status view Requester view field review Empty and stale states Empty and stale state validation Requester access verification Requester-only access results

For each selected item, record the question and its scope, approved inputs, hard stop condition, and reviewer.

Check that each selected child can work without waiting for another child's result. Keep shared dependencies with the parent or run dependent work in sequence.

docs.title: Step 2: Record the questions and limits
docs.text:
For each selected child:

  1. Move the item to the mapped active state.
  2. Add the question, scope, and stop condition to the description or a comment.
  3. Keep shared decisions in the parent item.

Use the project's existing state mapping. Check the item ID before every MCP or browser write.

docs.title: Step 3: Start GitHub Copilot orchestration
docs.text:
Build the parent instruction from the selected work items. Include each item ID, question and its scope, approved inputs, stop condition, and reviewer.

Start the work through /orchestrate. Check that GitHub Copilot created one live child session for each selected item. Use the orchestration surface to track the sessions. Do not copy live session identifiers into Boards.

Repository work must name the allowed repository and path. The child session may return evidence or a draft pull request when the contract allows it. It must not close the Boards item, approve a pull request, merge, deploy, or make the release decision.

docs.title: Step 4: Inspect and control the work
docs.text:
Inspect the live child sessions in GitHub Copilot. Use Azure Boards MCP or the browser to record progress.

Signal Action Work is safe and on scope Wait A safe result needs a specific correction Redirect A completed result is unusable or outside scope Reject Work crosses an access, data, usage, or authority boundary Stop The contract is met Accept

Record the control decisions you actually make. Stop unsafe work, reject unsupported claims, and escalate decisions that require human authority.

docs.title: Step 5: Review and update Boards
docs.text:
1. Add the decision and reason to the child item.
  2. Move accepted items to the project's reviewed or completed state.
  3. Keep revised items active with one clear correction.
  4. Move rejected items to the agreed closed state without approving their content.
  5. Stop unsafe work and record the boundary that ended it.

Return to Exercise 4 in ../README.md. Use the reviewed parent result to update the parent item only when that write is approved. Retrieve the item again to check the change.

docs.title: Safety boundaries
docs.text:
• Work only with the seeded training hierarchy.
  • Don't change process settings, team configuration, area paths, or iteration paths.
  • Don't put secrets, personal data, production records, or real organization names in work items.
  • Don't let an agent approve, merge, deploy, contact people, or close the parent decision.
  • Stop when an item requests restricted data or needs authority you don't have.

docs.title: Reset and cleanup
docs.text:
1. Restore each selected item to the starting state recorded during preflight.
  2. Remove only links, tags, or assignments that you added when project policy allows it.
  3. If a training comment cannot be removed, add a short cleanup note.
  4. Close the GitHub Copilot child sessions and follow the repository's branch or pull-request cleanup policy.
  5. Do not delete the seeded hierarchy unless the trainer gives a reset instruction for those exact item IDs.

If the trainer supplied a seed/reset tool, follow its README.

docs.title: Goal
docs.text:
Show learners how to direct four issue-based workstreams through live GitHub Copilot orchestration. The orchestration surface tracks the running work. The plan holds only the decisions needed before work starts.

Developers after Session M2-05 use the local PR-readiness route instead. It reviews implementation behavior, tests, and a supplied snapshot without GitHub MCP.

docs.text: Time Segment Outcome 0:00-0:10 Parent objective and workstream boundaries Split work without hidden dependencies. 0:10-0:20 Minimal workstream plan Set questions, inputs, stops, and reviewers. 0:20-0:32 Monitor and intervene Wait, redirect, stop, accept, reject, or escalate. 0:32-0:45 Live demonstration Review child sessions on the orchestration surface. 0:45-0:55 Review the parent result Keep supported findings and visible gaps. 0:55-1:00 Lab handoff Check access and deliverables.

docs.title: Prepare
docs.text:
• /orchestrate and the built-in orchestrate skill work.
  • Product route: GitHub MCP can read the selected issues.
  • Developer route: the supplied Python tests run and local project read access works.
  • You can open, redirect, and stop child sessions.
  • Use synthetic or sanitized work.

docs.title: Minimal workstream plan
docs.text:
Each workstream needs:

  • one question with a clear scope;
  • issue inputs;
  • one hard stop condition;
  • one reviewer.

Don't copy session links, status, timing, usage, or progress into the plan. GitHub Copilot already holds that state.

Workstream Question Approved input Stop condition Reviewer Public mapping Is the public mapping ready for approval? Mapping issue and linked sources Restricted data or invented states are required Product owner Requester status Is the issue ready for implementation review? Requester-status issue and linked sources An unsupported field or forecast is required Delivery reviewer Empty and stale states Are fallback states testable? Fallback-state issue and linked sources An unsupported commitment is required Service reviewer Access boundary Are requester-access results ready for review? Access issue and linked synthetic results Production or personal data is requested Privacy reviewer

docs.title: Monitor the live work
docs.text:
Use the current session management surface. Show learners why you wait, redirect, stop, accept, reject, or escalate.

Signal Action Safe and on scope Wait Safe work needs a precise correction Redirect A hard boundary is crossed Stop The result meets the plan Accept The result lacks support Reject Human authority is required Escalate

docs.title: Review the parent result
docs.text:
Check that the parent connects findings to live issues, shows rejected claims, names open gaps, and recommends the next follow-up. It must not publish or change source systems without approval.

Session M7-06 reads the live issues and the reviewed parent result. Don't copy them into a separate status record or handoff file.

docs.title: Developer demonstration
docs.text:
Use the developer route in lab/README.md with the same one-hour plan. Replace the four issue questions with implementation, tests, and PR-state questions from developer-orchestration-plan.md.

Before delivery:

  1. Copy the reference implementation and six tests from Session M2-05.
  2. Run the documented unittest command and keep the actual result.
  3. Read developer-review-brief.md and pr-snapshot.json.
  4. Check that child sessions can read the shared files without editing them or using the network.

Run /orchestrate with the accepted questions. Open each child on the app surface. Redirect the test reviewer to criterion 5 after its first answer, then inspect the revised answer rather than assuming the first was wrong.

Have the parent evaluate the provisional author note that green local tests make the PR ready. The snapshot has a failed required integration check and unresolved blocking thread R1. Those remain blockers even when local tests pass. Children may agree; never fabricate a disagreement.

Allow 25 minutes for the work split, 30 for live inspection, 35 for steering and reconciliation, and 30 for parent review. Grade the findings learners checked and how they redirected the work, not an exact child count or speedup.

Use lab/solution/developer-review-reference.md after the human review. It explains the source facts but can't replace live child results.

docs.title: Lab handoff
docs.text:
Learners submit:

  1. the orchestration plan;
  2. the live orchestration result;
  3. the result of a fresh GitHub read for any issue update.

For the developer route, require the plan and the app's reviewed parent result, including the redirection, rejected readiness claim, and observed usage. No issue update or Session M7-06 handoff.

For an Azure Boards delivery, use the trainer supplement. GitHub Copilot still performs the orchestration.

docs.title: Session M7-06: Automate delivery follow-up and connect work systems
docs.text:
Open slides Slides in new tab Download PDF Close slides

Module: Product and Delivery Teams

Difficulty: Intermediate

Prerequisites: Sessions M7-01 to M7-05, GitHub Copilot app Automations access, and GitHub MCP access

Duration: 3 hours (1 hour trainer content + 2 hours lab)

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
Build one draft-only automation from the reviewed Session M7-05 result. It reads live GitHub issues and the parent orchestration result, then drafts a stakeholder update for human review.

Run the automation, update one issue, and run it again. Compare the results on the platform before finishing the stakeholder update. Scheduling stays disabled.

docs.title: Learning outcomes
docs.text:
• Define an automation's inputs, output, and limits in a short table.
  • Use live GitHub issues and the parent orchestration result as inputs.
  • Restrict the automation to one draft stakeholder update.
  • Review run records on the platform.
  • Rerun after an issue change.
  • Decide whether to keep, revise, disable, or pause the automation.
  • Name the authoritative planning system.

docs.title: Materials
docs.text: Resource Location Trainer guide trainer-content/README.md Slides slides.md Lab lab/README.md Starter assets lab/starter/ Reference solution lab/solution/

docs.title: Boundaries
docs.text:
• The automation reads only the GitHub issues and the Session M7-05 parent result.
  • Its only output is a draft stakeholder update.
  • It can't publish, message people, edit issues, change labels, or write to external systems.
  • A person reviews every draft.
  • The enabled or disabled state matches the definition.

docs.title: Optional Azure Boards route
docs.text: When Azure Boards is authoritative, use Boards items and the Session M7-05 parent result as inputs. Keep the output draft only. Don't keep competing status fields in GitHub and Azure Boards.

docs.title: Product and Delivery Teams | Intermediate

docs.title: Start from authoritative state
docs.text:
Use:

  • the live GitHub issues;
  • the reviewed Session M7-05 parent result.

Skip static handoffs. They drift from the platform state.

docs.title: Define the automation
docs.text: Field Decision Trigger and cadence Manual; no schedule Authoritative inputs Live issues and parent result Permitted output One draft stakeholder update Prohibited side effects No posts, messages, edits, or external writes Reviewer Named human role Stop conditions Named hard boundaries Current state Enabled or disabled

docs.title: Review run details on the platform
docs.text: Inspect run status, identifiers, timing, usage, and supporting results on the platform.

docs.title: Create one manual automation
docs.text:
Read the approved status-visibility GitHub issues and the reviewed Session M7-05
parent result. Draft one stakeholder update from supported issue state. Name
unresolved exceptions and owners. Do not publish or change systems.

Use the minimum GitHub read tools.

docs.title: Review the first run
docs.text:
• Trace every claim to an issue or the parent result.
  • Keep gaps or conflicts in the source information visible.
  • Reject unsupported causes and forecasts.
  • Check that no prohibited side effect occurred.
  • Choose Keep, Revise, Disable, or Pause.

docs.title: Change one approved input
docs.text:
Update the requester-access training issue with the approved synthetic results.

Retrieve the issue again. Then run the same automation.

Check that the new draft differs only because of the approved issue change.

docs.title: Stakeholder update
docs.text:
State:

  • the reporting scope;
  • supported status changes;
  • unresolved exceptions and owners;
  • the review decision;
  • the next action.

A person shares the update.

docs.title: Choose one authoritative system
docs.text:
Use GitHub when issues and agent work live there.

Use Azure Boards when the delivery backlog lives there.

Do not maintain competing status fields.

docs.title: Scheduling stays disabled
docs.text:
The core lab uses supervised manual runs.

Enable a cadence only after separate sign-off. Update the current state when the automation is enabled or disabled.

1. Concise automation definition
  2. Reviewed stakeholder update

Run records stay on the platform.

docs.title: Lab
docs.text: Overview Lab Trainer Guide

docs.title: Session M7-06 lab: Create and review a delivery automation
docs.text:
Duration: 2 hours

Difficulty: Intermediate

Prerequisites: Sessions M7-01 to M7-05, Automations access, and GitHub MCP access

docs.title: Outcome
docs.text:
Create one automation that reads the live GitHub issues and the reviewed Session M7-05 parent result. Review its first draft, apply one issue change, and run it again. Compare the drafts to see how that change affected the update. You end with the automation definition and one reviewed stakeholder update.

The core lab uses a manual trigger and draft-only output. Scheduling stays disabled.

Part Work Time 1 Check access and retrieve inputs 20 min 2 Complete the automation definition 20 min 3 Create and run the automation 30 min 4 Review the draft 20 min 5 Update one issue and rerun 20 min 6 Finalize the stakeholder update 10 min

docs.title: Before you start
docs.text: Complete the track capability setup.

docs.title: Part 1: Check access and retrieve inputs
docs.text:
1. Open Automations in the GitHub Copilot app.
  2. Check that New automation is available.
  3. Retrieve the parent and child GitHub issues through GitHub MCP.
  4. Open the reviewed Session M7-05 parent orchestration result.
  5. Check that issue state and the parent result agree on the four workstreams.

docs.title: Part 2: Complete the automation definition
docs.text:
Copy starter/automation-definition-template.md into your working folder.

Complete only these fields:

  • trigger and cadence;
  • authoritative inputs;
  • permitted output;
  • prohibited side effects;
  • reviewer;
  • stop conditions;
  • current enabled or disabled state.

In your definition, use a manual trigger and limit the output to one draft stakeholder update. Enable the automation only for supervised lab runs.

docs.title: Part 3: Create and run the automation
docs.text:
Create a local automation with the minimum GitHub read tools.

Use this prompt:

Read the approved status-visibility GitHub issues and the reviewed Session M7-05
parent orchestration result. Follow @automation-definition-template.md. Draft one
stakeholder update from supported issue state. Name unresolved exceptions and
owners. Do not publish, message people, edit issues, change labels, call
unapproved tools, or invent missing values.

Review the trigger, tools, prompt, and enabled state before the run. Keep any schedule disabled.

docs.title: Part 4: Review the draft
docs.text:
Inspect the run on the Automations surface.

Check that:

  • each status claim traces to a live issue or the reviewed parent result;
  • gaps or conflicts in the source information remain visible;
  • no unsupported cause or forecast appears;
  • no prohibited side effect occurred;
  • the output is one draft stakeholder update.

Choose Keep, Revise, Disable, or Pause. Update the definition's current state to match that decision.

docs.title: Part 5: Update one issue and rerun
docs.text:
Open starter/approved-input-change.md.

  1. Apply the synthetic update to the named training issue through a reviewed GitHub MCP write.
  2. Retrieve the issue again and check the new state.
  3. Run the same automation. Do not create a second automation.
  4. Compare the two runs on the Automations surface.
  5. Check that only the approved issue change explains the draft change.

docs.title: Part 6: Finalize the stakeholder update
docs.text:
Complete starter/stakeholder-update-template.md from the second reviewed draft.

The update must state:

  • the reporting scope;
  • supported status changes;
  • unresolved exceptions and owners;
  • the review decision;
  • the next action.

Name GitHub or Azure Boards as the authoritative planning system. A person shares the update, not the automation.

  • Each session's overview lists its own prerequisites. Open sessions from the module list.

docs.title: Track: Product and Delivery Teams
docs.text:
For: product managers, product owners, business analysts, project managers, and delivery leads Time: 18 hours, 6 sessions Delivery: 3 days

Learners use the GitHub Copilot app to work through one initiative, the fictional Service Request Portal. They gather context, settle product decisions, plan issues, build a planning canvas, supervise parallel reviews, and draft a follow-up. The path is called Delivery Decision Studio. That's the curriculum's name, not a GitHub product.

No programming, Git command line, or repository administration skills needed. Keep the path no-code and use the supplied scenario. If you substitute your own, use synthetic, sanitized data with no customer names.

docs.title: Before you start
docs.text:
Learners need:

  • A GitHub account with Copilot access
  • The GitHub Copilot app and browser access to the training repository
  • GitHub MCP access to the training repository
  • Canvas creation, orchestration, and Automations access

Learners without Copilot access can't take this track. Reschedule them.

docs.title: Trainer setup
docs.text:
Do this before M7-01 and check the tools again before each session.

  1. Open the project. In the app, add the training repository under Projects, start a session, and ask Copilot to read one file.
  2. Check customizations. Open Customize → Installed and list the skills, MCP servers, plugins, and canvases. Installing a plugin doesn't prove GitHub MCP can read the repository, so test that separately.
  3. Check skills. M7-04 and M7-05 use the built-in /create-canvas and /orchestrate. Type / and confirm both appear. For M7-02, commit .github/skills/decision-interview/SKILL.md to the training repository, open a new session, and run /decision-interview with a test request. In the CLI, use /skills reload and /skills info decision-interview.
  4. Check GitHub MCP (M7-03 to M7-06). Open Customize → MCP → Installed, ask Copilot to list its GitHub tools, and read one thing from the repository. Don't start a write lab until the read works. In the CLI, use /mcp list and /mcp show github. Never paste tokens into prompts or files.
  5. Check session controls. Confirm the Interactive, Plan, and Autopilot modes; @, #, and / references; /context, /compact, /clear, and /rubber-duck. If a command is missing, note it and teach only what works.
Session Needs M7-01 App project and repository reads M7-02 Project skill decision-interview M7-03 GitHub MCP issue reads and writes M7-04 /create-canvas and GitHub MCP reads M7-05 /orchestrate, child-session steering, GitHub MCP M7-06 Automations and GitHub MCP

docs.title: Trainer notes
docs.text:
• Treat generated output as a proposal. A named person accepts, rejects, or revises it.
  • Keep customer and source organization names out of prompts, artifacts, issues, and screenshots.
  • Learners review generated extensions and tool calls. They don't write application code, MCP servers, plugins, or canvas extensions.

docs.title: Azure Boards supplement (trainer only)
docs.text:
Use Azure Boards only if your delivery plan calls for it, and prepare it before the workshop. Don't offer it as a learner alternative. scripts/azure-boards/README.md describes the tools that seed, check, and reset a synthetic Agile or Scrum backlog. They check existing project settings and never create them. The supplements need Copilot too:

  • M7-02 supplement: shape a seeded requirement
  • M7-05 supplement: supervise seeded workstreams
